ActiveAttackView.description:
Fleet-wide live threat board (E5, the security ops-lens reads this). One
per snapshot. `active` is false when only the always-on ambient internet
floor is present; `per_class` is still populated so the lens shows the
baseline. `per_class` is in fixed `AttackClass::all()` order.

`summary` / `components` are the FACILITY roll-up of every live attack;
`edges` lists each attack with the zone it lands on (one flood is one
zone's edge, so a two-zone site can carry two).

carrier_leak_gbps.description:
Site-total Volumetric upstream leak, from the Volumetric
`PositionalThreat.upstream_leaked` (attack leak plus ambient leak).
0 with no plan active.

carrier_scrubbed_gbps.description:
Site-total Volumetric upstream scrub, from the Volumetric
`PositionalThreat.upstream_scrubbed` (attack scrub PLUS the always-on
ambient floor's scrub). 0 with no plan active or no Volumetric
ambient/attack.

edges.description:
Every live attack, ascending by id, each naming its zone. Empty when
calm.

zones.description:
Per-zone flood readout for the Flood protection page's Zones section
One row per
ATTACKED zone, ascending `az_id`. Empty when calm. Derived from the
Volumetric class's positional resolution: scrubbing only ever
touches `AttackClass::Volumetric`, so this is not per-class.

appliance_kind.description:
Spec-aligned kind tag (`"firewall"` / `"ids"` / `"waf"` /
`"ddos_scrubber"` / `"vpn"` / `"loadbalancer"` / `"hsm"` /
`"siem"`). Selects the icon and tone.

az_id.description:
Availability zone this appliance sits in, so the security estate can be
scoped per AZ without re-deriving it from `rack_id`.
Resolved from the rack for a racked box, and from the HOST GATEWAY for
a `gateway_addon` (which has no rack of its own). 0 when neither
resolves.

dropped_per_sec.description:
Live filtering throughput, latest ring sample. ONE FIELD PER ATTACK
CLASS, in that class's own unit, never combined, and a dual-licensed
(Scrub + Firewall) box populates more than one:
- `dropped_per_sec`, stateful-firewall Protocol drops, **Kpps**
- `scrubbed_gbps`, scrubber Volumetric absorb, **Gbps**
- `events_per_sec`, IDS/IPS Intrusion detections, **events/s**

A box without the matching licence enabled reports 0 for that class.
Off-path kinds (HSM/SIEM) report 0 for all three. Abstract magnitudes
(spec §9.1).

egress_gbps.description:
Smoothed directional egress in Gbps (traffic leaving the
appliance toward the LAN side). Pairs with `ingress_gbps`.

enabled_functions.description:
Enabled security functions on this box as slugs ("firewall"/"ips"/
"scrub"), the base plus any licensed-on. Dynamic (changes only on a
license toggle). The console joins these with the catalog's per-SKU
license options (`ApplianceSkuView.licenses`) to render the toggle rows
+ costs, the static option data is NOT duplicated per tick.

fabric_capacity_gbps.description:
Nameplate forwarding ceiling, wire-rate throughput when the
inspection plane is bypassed. Compared against `fabric_load_gbps`.

fabric_load_gbps.description:
Smoothed full-duplex fabric load in Gbps (= `egress_gbps +
ingress_gbps`, independently smoothed). The saturation metric;
when this exceeds `fabric_capacity_gbps` the forwarding plane
drops packets regardless of inspection state.

fabric_saturated.description:
Forwarding-plane saturation edge: `fabric_load_gbps` over the appliance's
inspection-REDUCED effective forwarding capacity (deep inspection eats
forwarding headroom). Engine-computed in the appliance fabric pass for
IN-PATH inspectors that actually forward; an in-path box in this state
drops customer traffic transiting it (facility-wide, folded into the same
drop path as switch/uplink saturation) and fires an
`ApplianceFabricSaturated` event + incident on the rising edge, like
Switch/Gateway/Uplink. Off-path taps (HSM/SIEM) never forward, so this
stays false for them.

fabric_utilisation.description:
`fabric_load_gbps / forwarding_ceiling_gbps`. Folded ONCE in the projection from the SAME two
figures above, so the forwarding meter's fill fraction and the
engine's own saturation verdict cannot disagree. `[0, 1+]`, not
clamped. 0 when `forwarding_ceiling_gbps` is 0.

forwarding_ceiling_gbps.description:
The appliance's effective FORWARDING ceiling with deep inspection's
penalty applied, `fabric_load_gbps` is the load against it, and it IS
the threshold `fabric_saturated` flips on. **Keyed on the WAN UPLINK
CHAIN (`SecurityApplianceSku::wan_port_capacity_gbps`), not the raw ASIC
`fabric_capacity_gbps`**: a box cannot forward faster than its
narrowest WAN leg, and the engine's own verdict is WAN-capped via
`effective_ceiling_gbps`'s `ApplianceFabric` arm, so the readout agrees
with the flag beside it (on `fw_basic`, 20 G ASIC and 11 G WAN pair, it
reads 11.0). Collapses toward `inspection_capacity_gbps` as
inspection engages. Mirrors `GatewayView::forwarding_ceiling_gbps` (same
shared curve, `sim_core::security::effective_forwarding_capacity_gbps`,
same reason: a client dividing `fabric_load_gbps` by a nameplate
disagreed with the engine's own saturation verdict). Never re-derive it
renderer-side.

gateway_addon.description:
True for gateway ADD-ONS (`ApplianceMount::GatewayAddon`), license
modules living inside a gateway, not racked boxes. They have no
rack position, no ports, and (since the addon-mitigation fold)
their per-class work is attributed to the HOST GATEWAY's defender
entry, so their own drop/event meters legitimately read 0.
Standalone-appliance UI (the IDS performance board, SIEM presence,
rack rendering) must skip these, the gateway console owns their
presentation.

ingress_gbps.description:
Smoothed directional ingress in Gbps (traffic arriving from the
WAN side). Mirror of `egress_gbps`.

inspection_capacity_gbps.description:
Rated DPI ceiling (Gbps). Typically a fraction of
`fabric_capacity_gbps`, e.g. a 10 G appliance might inspect
at 3 G. When `inspection_enabled` is true and live throughput
exceeds this, the appliance either bypasses (drops to forwarding
rate) or drops packets, depending on `inspection_state`.

inspection_enabled.description:
Whether deep inspection is currently on (the bypass lever, toggled by
`SetApplianceInspection`).

inspection_load_gbps.description:
Smoothed live throughput **actually deep-inspected**. Distinct
from `egress_gbps` (total pass-through). When inspection is
bypassed this is 0 even while pass-through is high.

inspection_saturated.description:
Edge-triggered: `inspection_load_gbps > inspection_capacity_gbps`.
Even when fabric still has headroom, this fires when the DPI
engine itself overloads.

inspection_state.description:
`"Active"` (inspecting), `"Bypass"` (line-rate forwarding, no
inspection), or `"Failed"` (engine forced drop, DPI overload).
Drives the inspection-plane LED color on the appliance pill.

inspection_utilisation.description:
`inspection_load_gbps / inspection_capacity_gbps`, folded ONCE in the
projection so the DPI meter's
fill fraction and `inspection_saturated` cannot disagree. `[0, 1+]`,
not clamped. 0 when `inspection_capacity_gbps` is 0 (off-path boxes,
or a kind with no DPI plane).

inv_status.description:
Lifecycle status, see `HostView::inv_status`. Reads `"Mounted"`,
`"Carried"` or `"Loose"`.

The row is always present, so presence in this array does NOT mean
"racked": this field is the location. Pair it with `carried_by`, never
one half: `carried_by` is 0 for nobody AND 0 is a valid seat.

Four-corner parity with Host / Switch / PatchPanel.

monthly_opex_dollars.description:
Live projected monthly opex ($/mo), running fee + chassis power +
seated-optic draw. Mirrors the host console's read.

owned_functions.description:
Function-license slugs whose one-time capex has already been paid on this
box (the ownership ledger, superset of `enabled_functions`). An owned
license that's been unsubscribed (not in `enabled_functions`) can be
re-enabled for FREE; the console reads this to show `Resubscribe (free)`
vs `Buy $X`.

ports.description:
Per-port views, one entry per physical port on the appliance.
Same shape as `SwitchView.ports` and `GatewayView.ports`. Each port
carries media, state, link capacity, live throughput and a peer
reference.

power_feeds.description:
Connected AC cord count. >= 2 = PSU-failure resilience at
`redundant_psu_overhead_w` extra draw per extra cord.

powered.description:
At least one AC cord seated (or none required). False = dark
until the player plugs it in. Mirrors the engine's `powered`.

psu_dark.description:
True when no corded PSU can deliver power: every lamp reads dark,
`indicator` forced `Off` alongside it. See `HostVisual.psu_dark`.

threats.description:
Per-device threat handling, ONLY the classes THIS box defends, with
what reached it, what it absorbed, and what it passed on. Replaces the
confusing fleet-wide read: a firewall shows Protocol only, an IDS shows
Intrusion only. Empty for off-path boxes (HSM / SIEM). From the engine
positional cascade.

AttackComponentView.description: One vector of the current composed attack.

AttackEdgeView.description: One live attack on one zone's internet edge.

az_id.description: The zone whose edge the flood arrives on.

ends_at_ns.description: Sim-time the attack ends on its own.

summary.description: Eng-voice "vector magnitude + vector magnitude" line for this attack.

target_customer_id.description: The tenant that drew the fire, 0 for an unsolicited flood.

AttackZoneView.description:
One zone's share of the live flood, for the Flood protection page's Zones
table. `aimed_gbps` is what the attack actually threw at this zone
(`arrived_gbps + scrubbed_upstream_gbps`); `scrubbed_upstream_gbps` is what
a carrier-side `sim_core::scrub::ScrubPlan` removed before the line ever
saw it; `arrived_gbps` is what reached this zone's lines (leak + any
cover overflow), the same figure `ThreatClassView.incoming` folds into the
fleet total for Volumetric.

AzTrunkView.description:
One inter-zone trunk: the virtual fibre between two zones of one region,
with a LANE each way. Cross-zone east-west, database
replication and egress failover ride it per crossing; a pair whose trunk
is down reroutes through a third zone or partitions. `a < b` always, so
the `ab_*` lane runs from the lower zone id to the higher and `ba_*` the
other way. Per-tick `EntityDelta`-carried section `az_trunks` (see
`DeltaSnapshot::az_trunks`), one row per zone pair
in a region. The REST by-id form (`/api/v1/network/trunks/{id}`) and the
wire delta's `EntityDelta::removed` both address a trunk as `a * 65536 +
b` (the two zone ids, `a < b`) via [`az_trunk_key`], since a pair has no
id of its own.

a.description: The lower zone id of the pair.

ab_drop_p.description: Drop probability the `a` to `b` lane applies to what crosses it.

ab_gbps.description: Smoothed load on the lane from `a` to `b` (Gbps).

ab_saturated.description: The `a` to `b` lane is over its capacity (with the anti-flap band).

b.description: The higher zone id of the pair.

ba_drop_p.description: Drop probability the `b` to `a` lane applies to what crosses it.

ba_gbps.description: Smoothed load on the lane from `b` to `a` (Gbps).

ba_saturated.description: The `b` to `a` lane is over its capacity.

capacity_gbps.description: Capacity of each lane (Gbps), the site's per-pair figure.

up.description:
Both zones have a live, data-cabled multi-zone router and the trunk is
not cut. A down trunk carries nothing; its lanes read their residual.

BuildingOfferView.description: One building's cage state, for the relocate panel's per-building rows.

az_id.description: The AZ this building is, when it has been bought. 0 while unowned.

az_name.description: Display name of that AZ ("AZ-1"), empty while unowned.

can_buy_cage.description: A cage can be bought here right now: owned, not full, affordable.

slots.description: Floor slots live in this building (`cages_owned * slots_per_cage`).

BusinessPolicyView.description:
Company-wide business policy mirror (see `business_policy::BusinessPolicy`).
Surfaced in the Business area, not the operational Services page.

CableEndpointView.description:
Tagged endpoint reference used by the generalized cable model. Mirrors
`sim_core::cable::CableEndpoint` but with bare ids (no newtypes) so the
JSON shape stays simple for the frontend / FFI layer.

Every DEVICE-PORT variant carries its render identity (`anchor` +
`anchor_ordinal`) beside the engine `port` index, see [`PortAnchorView`]
for why the index alone cannot name an anchor. `RackPower` does NOT: it is
not a device port at all (which is why it carries `feed`, not `port`), its
anchor is synthesized from the rack, and giving it a family would put a
variant on the wire that nothing consumes.

oneOf.description:
Rack-side end of an IEC power cord, the implied feed the lead
disappears into down the left manager strip. `feed` is the
per-rack cord ordinal.

RackPower.description:
Rack-side end of an IEC power cord, the implied feed the lead
disappears into down the left manager strip. `feed` is the
per-rack cord ordinal.

CableLane.description:
A bundling lane on a rack manager strip. Cables sharing a `(side,
u_band, lane)` triple stack along the lane in slot order. Power,
copper, twinax and fibre each occupy their own lane, so they draw as
distinct bundles, as in real cable management.

The engine assigns the lane at lay time from `CableKind::lane()`. The
player never picks it.

breakout_id.description:
Breakout membership. Legs sharing this id fan out from one QSFP
trunk port, the renderer draws a single trunk run that splits to
each leg's far port. `None` = ordinary point-to-point cable.
(Tiny `Option<u32>` mirror of `lag_id`; delta/capnp treat it like
any other scalar, no per-tick allocation.)

color.description:
Player-chosen jacket colour id ("Orange" / "Blue" / …). Always a
concrete colour, the projection resolves the cable's stored choice
or its family default, so the renderer paints off it directly
(`Tokens.cable_color_for_choice`). Empty only on legacy wire frames.

dac_class.description: Twinax class ("Passive" / "Active"). Only meaningful for DAC kinds.

duplex.description:
True for LC-duplex fibre patch cords (TX/RX strand pair). The
renderer draws two parallel strands; everything else is one tube.
Read directly off the cable view, no catalog/timing dependency.

Purely `CableKind::is_duplex()`, the property of the cable itself. Cage
geometry (an SFP-to-QSFP run is duplex at the SFP end) travels in
[`Self::qsfp_end`] instead.

from_host.description:
Legacy host↔switch fields. Populated for host-link cables for
back-compat with the pre-Phase-B renderer. New cable types
(switch↔edd, future player-laid) leave these as 0.

id.description:
Generalized endpoint metadata (Phase B+). Populated for *all* cables
going forward, including host-links. Renderers should prefer reading
`a` / `b` over the legacy `from_host` / `to_switch` fields.

is_failed.description:
True iff this cable is currently in a transient failed state
(`Cable::is_failed(now)`, gates traffic engine-side). Renderer
colours failed cables red.

lag_id.description:
LAG (link aggregation) membership. Cables sharing this id form a
bonded link. `None` = standalone cable.

mode_pinned.description:
`true` when the player pinned this link's mode in the console (so
it's not auto-managed). `false` = Auto. With `routed` this gives the
console the tri-state Auto / L2 / L3.

path.description:
Full ordered anchor sequence the cable runs through, port A →
port B, `sim_core::cable::RouteAnchor`, THE one anchor
vocabulary (client-send, engine-store, engine-emit). First and
last anchor are always `Port`. Middle anchors describe in-rack
management (`Strip`), rack-edge transitions (`Edge`),
side-panel rail holes (`RailHole`), and inter-rack runs
(`Tray`). This is already the FULL resolved route, the engine
expands strip runs into their marker/channel sequence
(`expand_strip_chains_rack`) before emitting, so the renderer
only ever draws between consecutive anchors, never re-derives
which ones to visit. When this is shorter than 3 entries (just
the two endpoint ports), the renderer treats the cable as
freely draped, same as the legacy `routed_via.is_empty()` case.

qsfp_end.description:
Which END sits in a QSFP (multi-lane) cage: `0` neither, `1` = a,
`2` = b, `3` = both. A QSFP cage presents one `qsfp_module.glb`
connector with a single boot, so the duplex strand pair converges
there, the same 2-into-1 the renderer already does at a fibre patch
panel. `3` means converge at both ends, i.e. render as one tube, which
is correct for an MPO trunk between two QSFP cages.

Zero is "neither" deliberately: `CableView` derives [`Default`] and the
field is `#[serde(default)]`, so a default-constructed view lands on the
plain-tube value. A `-1` sentinel would default to `0` and silently
claim end "a".

route_slots.description:
Per-segment bundle slot, same length as `routed_via`. Each entry
is this cable's slot index (0-based) inside the corresponding tray
segment, computed deterministically by sorting cable ids that share
the segment. Renderer combines slot + tray cross-section + layout
pattern into a lateral offset so cables don't visually overlap.

routed.description:
`true` when this inter-switch link runs L3/Routed (ECMP) vs L2/
Bridged (STP). Authoritative owner is `Cable.link_mode`. Lets the
switch console show + toggle each link's forwarding mode.

routed_via.description:
Tray segments / hooks / risers this cable runs through, in order
from `a` to `b`. Empty = draped (no managed path).

CageOfferView.description:
Live cage-expansion state for the current site, carried on the per-tick
keyframe (the static cage geometry is on `SiteSpecView`). Drives the
colo "buy cage" shop button: enabled iff `uses_cages && !at_max &&
affordable`. `next_cage_label` is the pre-formatted button caption
("Buy cage 2 of 8" / "All cages owned").

affordable.description: Player can afford the next cage right now.

at_max.description: All cages already owned, nothing left to buy.

building_affordable.description: Another building is available and affordable right now.

building_price_dollars.description:
Price of the next BUILDING, dollars. Distinct from `price_dollars`,
which is a cage: they are two purchases, not one.

buildings.description:
One row per BUILDING at a multi-building site; empty everywhere else.

Cages are owned per building and bought in any order, so "cages owned"
is not one number at a campus and the panel needs a row each.

buildings_owned.description: Buildings owned. 1 at a single-room site.

buildings_total.description: Buildings this site has in total. 1 at a single-room site.

price_dollars.description: Price of the next cage, dollars.

uses_cages.description:
This site expands by cages (colo). `false` at flat sites, the client
hides the buy-cage affordance entirely.

CandidateCauseView.description:
One ranked candidate cause on an incident: the specific fault hypothesis
(the failing hop the forwarding graph names), how confident the engine is,
whether it's confirmed, and its own per-cause guidance + codex links.

article_ids.description:
Codex article ids for this cause's mechanic; titles resolve
client-side, as for `IncidentView::article_ids`.

cleared.description:
This cause's fault has since cleared, but the symptom is still open,
a tenant's rolling p99 keeps reading high after the cause is gone. The
candidate is retained (not deleted) so a pinned cause is never silently
retracted; the client renders it muted as "cleared", offers no repair,
and does not fall back to "cause not yet identified".

confidence.description: 0..=100 confidence this is the real cause.

confirmed.description: Player- or engine-confirmed as the real cause.

entity_id.description: Primary entity id from the cause (host/cable/switch id). 0 for global.

msg_key.description:
Localization key for the cause label, `incident-<root_kind-kebab>`,
the same key space as `IncidentView::root_msg_key` (a candidate cause
IS a root hypothesis). Empty until keyed; render `label*` then.

rack_id.description: Rack the cause's beacon should mark; 0 when nothing is racked.

CapacityView.description:
Capacity + burn-rate projection. Drives the dashboard's Capacity tab.
`monthly_burn_dollars` is the *current operating rate*, not an average
over history, it answers "if nothing changes, what does this month
cost?" `months_until_cash_out` uses (burn − revenue) so a profitable
op reports a very large runway sentinel (renderer formats it as "∞").

cash_minute.description:
Cash balance sampled once per simulated minute. 60-deep ring,
"last hour" sparkline on the Money lens. Log-encoded via
`q_gbps_log` (unit-agnostic: mantissa × 10^exp).

cost_minute.description:
Cost delta per simulated minute. Pairs with `revenue_minute` for
the Money lens net-flow trend.

free_power_w.description:
Power headroom in watts (cooling capacity − heat load). Clamped
at 0 if heat exceeds cooling (over-budget facility).

free_vcpu_milli.description:
COMMITTED-basis headroom: nameplate minus placed allocation minus the
service-plane reservation, per host, floored at 0.

**NOT the complement of `used_vcpu_milli`.** `free` answers "what could
I still place", `used` answers "what is being consumed right now", and
they are computed from different quantities: `used + free != total`,
and `total - used` is not free capacity. The full three-way
relationship, and why there is no ordering invariant between them, is on
[`CapacityView::used_vcpu_milli`]. Read it before doing arithmetic
across the two.

largest_free_vcpu_milli.description:
Largest free single-host slot across serviceable hosts (after failover
headroom): the biggest VM that could actually be seated right now.
The Capacity lens shows this vs the requested spec so a
`FleetCapacityExhausted` shortfall reads as "fragmented, add a host".

largest_free_vgpu_slices.description:
Largest free vGPU partition on any SINGLE serviceable host: the biggest
slice ask the fleet could seat right now.

`free_vgpu_slices` is a fleet SUM and is therefore blind to
fragmentation: twelve hosts holding 2 free slices each report "24 free"
while a 4-slice VM cannot place anywhere. Show BOTH: the sum is what you
own, this is what you can actually hand to one VM.

monthly_burn_dollars.description: Projected monthly cost at the current operating rate.

monthly_revenue_dollars.description:
Projected monthly revenue at the current operating rate (last
hour × `tuning.hours_per_month`, the SAME month `monthly_burn_dollars`
is denominated in). Computed from
recurring billing only, one-time signup bonuses and prepay credits are
excluded so accepting a prospect doesn't briefly extrapolate into a
phantom monthly.

months_until_cash_out.description:
`cash / max(0, burn − revenue)`, with a 1e9-month sentinel (never
`f64::INFINITY`, serde encodes that as JSON null) when revenue covers
burn. A renderer must label that sentinel by the SIGN of the surplus:
revenue EXCEEDING cost is profitable, not break-even.

The `burn` in that denominator is the CASH burn:
`monthly_burn_dollars` less [`CostRatesView::depreciation_dollars`],
NOT `monthly_burn_dollars` itself. Depreciation is a real operating cost
but it never moves the balance (`CostKind::settles_in_cash()` is false),
so charging it against the runway makes a fleet that owns its hardware
look closer to broke than it is. The P&L figure and the cash figure are
deliberately two numbers; do not re-derive this one from the other.

revenue_minute.description:
Revenue *delta* per simulated minute (charged this minute).
Same encoding + cap as `cash_minute`.

service_reserved_vcpu_milli.description:
Compute the service plane (control planes + agents) is holding: the
overhead of running your services, surfaced for transparency.

total_gpu_mem_mb.description:
Fleet GPU frame-buffer capacity (MB) across serviceable GPU hosts, and
the largest free block on any single host.

Frame buffer is the SECOND vGPU bound and frequently the BINDING one: a
32 GB/VM tenant on a `gpu_2x_2u` (8 slices, 48 GB) seats ONE VM, not the
two its slice count implies.

total_vcpu_milli.description:
Fleet compute + storage: what you actually HAVE, so the prospect card
can show "free vs. needed" in absolute terms (not just an after-%).
`free_*` already nets out VM usage **and** service-plane overhead.
u64 because at hyperscale these exceed u32.

total_vgpu_slices.description:
Fleet vGPU partition capacity across every GPU host (`Host::total_vgpu_
slices` / `free_vgpu_slices`). 0 on a fleet with no GPU hardware. Lets
the prospect card show a GPU meter and answer "can I serve a GPU tenant"
in absolute slices, not just an after-%.

unplaceable_unit_count.description:
Total contracted CAPACITY the fleet cannot seat right now, summed
across every customer AND every service class they buy, VMs, database
copies, cluster workers, CDN POPs, LB proxies, object-store copies,
function capacity.

Counts every service class, so a tenant whose load balancer, CDN,
bucket or Kubernetes cluster cannot place contributes here too.

"Cannot be seated" means the probe's reason is a capacity/feasibility
one (`Engine::probe_reason_blocks_placement`). Capacity that is merely
waiting for the next ensure pass, and units whose hosts are down, are
deliberately NOT counted: this number answers "must I change the
fleet", not "is anything unhappy".

used_ssd_iops.description:
LIVE fleet storage demand in IOPS, and its WEAR-ADJUSTED ceiling.

The pair travels together so a client need not sum
`HostView::iops_capacity` itself. `total_ssd_iops` is summed from
`Host::eff_ssd_iops()`, the same accessor `HostView::iops_capacity` is
projected from, so an aged fleet cannot hide behind its as-bought IOPS.

`used_ssd_iops` is on the rotated telemetry half for the same reason
`used_vcpu_milli` is: its numerator rotates while its denominator moves
only on a host's install anniversary.

SAME NAMING HAZARD AS THE CPU PAIR: this struct carries no
`free_ssd_iops`, so there is nothing that looks like a complement. `used_ssd_iops` is live demand and `total_ssd_iops` is a
wear-adjusted ceiling; demand may exceed it, which is what storage
contention IS. Do not derive headroom by subtracting.

used_vcpu_milli.description:
LIVE fleet CPU demand in millivcpu: the world-scope numerator for
`used_vcpu_milli / total_vcpu_milli`, which is LOAD, a different question
from the COMMITTED `(total - free) / total` the same struct answers.

It is here rather than folded client-side because `HostView::
used_millivcpu` sits on the host TELEMETRY fingerprint half, so a host
outside the session's `DetailScope::near_racks` refreshes one tick in
`FAR_TELEMETRY_STRIDE` (64). A client sum therefore adds per-host samples
up to 16 SIMULATED MINUTES apart in age, against a denominator that does
not rotate, so the ratio drifts as the two halves age apart, and two
players standing in different rooms read different fleet CPU off one
world. `CustomersSummary`'s aggregates exist for the same reason.

NAMEPLATE BASIS, matching `total_vcpu_milli`: wear scales storage IOPS
only, so there is no worn CPU ceiling to divide by.

# `used_` AND `free_` ARE NOT COMPLEMENTS. THREE QUANTITIES, NOT TWO.

They sit side by side on this struct and read like a pair. They are not,
and the arithmetic a reader would write if they believed the names is
wrong with no failure to announce it:

```text
total - free  =  SUM over serviceable h of
                   min(committed_millivcpu + service_reserved_millivcpu,
                       eff_millivcpu)          <- COMMITTED ALLOCATION
used          =  SUM over serviceable h of used_millivcpu_total
                                             <- LIVE DEMAND
```

`Host::free_millivcpu` nets COMMITTED allocation and the service-plane
reservation, with a per-host `saturating_sub`, so on an overcommitted
host `free` floors at 0 and `total - free` is the host's whole ceiling
rather than what was committed on it.

**THERE IS NO ORDERING INVARIANT AND `used <= total` IS FALSE.**
`used_millivcpu_total` is demand and is deliberately NOT clamped to the
ceiling when a host has load (`traffic_sampling.rs`, the `load_demand
== 0` arm clamps, the loaded arm does not): `actual > phys` is the
DEFINITION of CPU contention, so a contended fleet legitimately reports
`used_vcpu_milli > total_vcpu_milli` and a ratio above 1.0. Any code
asserting or relying on the ordering is wrong about the domain, not
about the wire.

So: never write `total - used` and call it free, never write
`used + free` and call it total. Held by
`test_capacity_used_and_free_are_not_complements`.

ComponentView.description:
One installed part (PSU / disk / fan / DIMM / CPU) in a rack device, as
the device console's Repair tab shows it: what it is, how it is, and
where its replacement is. One row per part; two dead PSUs are two rows.

The delivery bar and the repair countdown are drawn CLIENT-side from the
two `*_ns` pairs against the `sim_time_ns` every delta already carries,
so an open tab costs the engine nothing between polls.

component_id.description:
The part's id, what `OrderPart` / `CancelPartOrder` / `RepairPart`
name. Stable across a swap (the part is reset in place).

life_hours.description:
This part's mean life in wear-hours (the owner SKU's MTBF times the
kind's `life_factor`, fixed at mint). Paired with `age_hours` for the
Repair tab's "age 120 h · rated ~9, 000 h" line. Mirrors
`sim_core::component::Component.life_hours`.

order_placed_at_ns.description: Delivery bar ends, sim nanoseconds. `0` when nothing is ordered.

order_state.description:
Where the replacement is: `"None"` (nothing ordered), `"Ordered"`
(in transit; `order_*_ns` are set), `"Arrived"` (on site, Repair is
available), `"Repairing"` (a swap work order is running;
`repair_*_ns` are set).

repair_started_at_ns.description: Repair countdown ends, sim nanoseconds. `0` when no swap is running.

replacement_dollars.description:
What Order replacement will charge, catalog price before macro
multipliers. `0` when no catalog row fits the part.

swap_count.description:
How many times this bay has had its part replaced. `0` = never
swapped, so the tab's "replaced N×" note is omitted. Mirrors
`sim_core::component::Component.swap_count`.

CostBreakdownView.description:
Lifetime spend ledger projected from `Engine::cost_breakdown`. All
fields are running totals in dollars.

# A purchase is not a cost, so this view describes TWO quantities

The asset ledger keeps capital purchases out of `Engine::total_cost`:
`acquire_asset` books capex to `Engine::total_capex` plus an asset row and
never touches `total_cost`, and what a purchase contributes to the P&L is
the `CostKind::Depreciation` charged off that ledger every billing tick.

So "a naive sum over these fields equals `topbar.total_cost_dollars`" is
**false.** The sum is `total_cost + total_capex - total_asset_disposal`. Which term a
bucket lands in is decided once, in `CostBreakdown::split`, and the three
results ride this view as `total_recurring_dollars` /
`total_capex_dollars` / `total_asset_disposal_dollars`. A UI that wants
"what have I spent operating the business" reads `total_recurring_dollars`;
one that wants "what have I sunk into hardware" reads
`total_capex_dollars`. Adding them together is a category error.

**Backward-looking only.** What next month COSTS is `CostRatesView`, a
separate struct on purpose: a rate derived from accumulated spend drifts
tick to tick even for a config constant such as facility rent.

One field per `CostBreakdown` bucket, no exceptions. `build_cost_breakdown`
destructures the engine struct exhaustively, so a new bucket is a compile
error until it lands here too.

asset_disposal_dollars.description:
Proceeds from selling / refunding / liquidating owned hardware, held
NEGATIVE because it is the reversal of a capital conversion, not a cost.
`total_asset_disposal_dollars` carries the same figure POSITIVE, which
is the one to render; do not "fix" the sign here, see
`CostBreakdown::asset_disposal`.

component_capex_dollars.description: Spares / replacement components ordered from the vendor.

eviction_fee_dollars.description: Break fee the operator pays to evict a tenant.

peering_monthly_dollars.description: Monthly opex on established peering relationships.

scrub_monthly_dollars.description:
Carrier-side flood protection: plan tier fee + clean-GB metering
(`CostKind::ScrubPlanMonth` + `ScrubCleanGb`). `#[serde(default)]`:
0 for a save with no plan.

service_unlock_dollars.description: One-time cost to light up a locked service class.

sla_credits_dollars.description:
SLA availability credits + latency penalties settled back to tenants.

Reads the engine's `cost_breakdown.sla_credits` BUCKET, which keeps the
credits of tenants that have churned.

staff_severance_dollars.description:
Severance paid when firing staff. Separate from `staff_signing`: a
hiring bonus and a redundancy payout are opposite events.

total_asset_disposal_dollars.description:
`Engine::total_asset_disposal`: lifetime proceeds from selling,
refunding or liquidating owned hardware, as a POSITIVE figure. Net
capital outlay is `total_capex_dollars - total_asset_disposal_dollars`.

total_capex_dollars.description:
`Engine::total_capex`: lifetime CAPITAL spend, cash converted into
owned things. Equals the sum of the capex buckets above (`host_capex`
… `uplink_activation_capex`), and NOT of the whole view: the "CapEx
(one-time)" section also holds `staff_signing` / `staff_severance` /
`service_unlock`, which are one-time but buy no asset and so stay in
`total_recurring_dollars`.

total_depreciation_dollars.description:
`Engine::total_depreciation`: lifetime depreciation charged off the
asset ledger. **A memo figure: it is already inside
`total_recurring_dollars` and already inside the opex buckets it was
charged to** (`depreciation_bucket` routes host/component/module to
`host_hourly`, network gear to `switch_hourly`, rack/region/AZ/facility
to `facility_rent`, cable/breakout to `cable_opex`, uplink and peering
to their monthlies). Adding it to anything double-counts. It is on the
wire so the Finance tab can answer "what does owning this fleet cost me
in a month where I buy nothing".

total_recurring_dollars.description:
`Engine::total_cost`: lifetime spend on what the business CONSUMED,
and the exact figure `topbar.total_cost_dollars` carries.

**Excludes hardware purchases.** A player who just bought $25k of hosts
sees no movement here; they see it in `total_capex_dollars`, and they
see its P&L consequence arrive slowly as depreciation.

uplink_activation_capex_dollars.description:
Carrier activation NRC on a new or re-provisioned WAN circuit:
one-off, distinct from the circuit's recurring `uplink_monthly`.

CostRatesView.description:
What the business costs to run for one more month, per category, at TODAY's
state. The forward-looking twin of `CostBreakdownView`.

Projected straight from `Engine::monthly_cost_rates`, which prices one
month's metered quantities through the same `rate_cost` the charge pass
uses, so a rate here equals what the engine will actually bill, scalers
(opex lever, macro power/egress events) included. The renderer does NO
cost arithmetic of its own.

The `avg_*` fields are the exception, and are named to say so: those
categories are DISCRETE EVENTS with no rate (a penalty is not a monthly
bill), so they carry a trailing average over `elapsed_months` instead.
A UI that shows them must label them as estimates.

avg_egress_cost_dollars.description:
Upstream transit bought, averaged. Real per-tenant spend, but it varies
with traffic, so there is no forward RATE to quote.

avg_sla_credits_dollars.description: SLA credits settled back to tenants, averaged.

depreciation_dollars.description:
What owning the fleet costs per month in straight-line decline:
`CostKind::Depreciation` over the ledger's active capex.

**Already inside the rates above and inside `total_dollars`.** The
engine folds each asset class's depreciation into the running-cost
category that already describes it (`depreciation_bucket`), so this is
the "of which" figure, not a thirteenth row. Sum it with the others and
you count hardware decline twice.

It ships because capex is not in `total_cost`: this is the ONLY number
that says buying a $25k rack of hosts has an ongoing price. A month in
which the player buys nothing still carries it.

elapsed_months.description:
Sim months elapsed since the run started: the averaging window for
every `avg_*` field. Zero on a fresh run, in which case the averages
are all zero and a UI should show a dash rather than a number.

facility_rent_dollars.description:
Site rent. A CONSTANT for a given site: if this moves between ticks
while the site has not changed, something is deriving it again.

host_hourly_dollars.description:
Host SKU running fees PLUS the site's vendor-support contract, matching
what the `host_hourly` bucket accumulates.

power_bill_dollars.description: Electricity on MEASURED draw at the site's price.

service_debt_dollars.description: Amortised loan repayment, clamped to the outstanding balance.

switch_hourly_dollars.description: Switch + gateway + EDD SKU running fees.

total_dollars.description:
Sum of the real rates above (including `transit_egress_dollars`),
identical to `CapacityView::monthly_burn_dollars`, which reads this
same projection.

transit_egress_dollars.description:
Upstream transit bought for tenants' projected egress, per month.

Included so the Finance tab's burn and the customer-pane cost total
(`CostAttribution::total`) agree on what a month costs. The
backward-looking twin `CostBreakdownView` carries `egress_cost_dollars`.

Read from the SAME `CostAttribution` walk that produces the per-tenant
egress margin, never re-derived, so the two cannot drift.

CustomerDetailView.description:
Everything about a tenant that only the OPEN tenant's console reads.

These fields are not on `CustomerView`'s per-tick row because each one has
no fleet-wide reader at all, or its only reader is `customer_detail.gd` /
`requirement_chips.gd`, both of which run for ONE tenant at a time, behind a
subscription that already exists.

**The reason is bytes.** The wire encodes `WorldSnapshot` with
`rmp_serde::to_vec_named`, so every field NAME is repeated on every one of
the roster's rows, and on a large roster the field names are the larger half
of the cost. Withholding a nested struct costs ONE absent key, so the saving
is the values AND their names.

**What is NOT here, and why, because the reasons are the design.**
`threat_exposure_weight` / `threat_targeted` stay on the row:
`security_view.gd` `_paint_exposure` ranks and totals EVERY tenant, so a
top-N cannot serve it and withholding the field would delete the exposure
panel. `availability_pct`, `p50/p99/p99_recent`, `rps` and `margin_dollars`
stay: `_customer_detail_columns` appends them for the whole visible roster,
and a per-tenant fetch would be N round trips at 4 Hz. `unit_count` /
`max_units_on_host` stay: `services_view.gd` rolls them up fleet-wide.
`archetype` stays because `_paint_header` runs on the WITHHELD path, so
moving it would blank the header subtitle for the tick or two a
subscription takes to land. `revenue_total_dollars`, `egress_gbps` and
`ingress_gbps` live here, and their fleet lenses are served instead by the
exact engine-built rankings on [`CustomersSummary`].

attack_class.description:
The attack class hitting this tenant (Flood / Connection flood / App flood
/ Break-in attempts), empty when not under attack, for the pill caption.
The BOOL (`CustomerView::under_attack`) stays on the row; only the prose
moved.

block_quality.description: Placement-quality score for the blocks this tenant sits on.

compliance_required.description:
Compliance regime the customer's contract requires (SOC2/HIPAA/PCI), or
"None". Mirrors `ProspectView.compliance_required`.

contract_grain.description:
The grain the CONTRACT holds this tenant to on its own
(`Engine::customer_contract_grain` tag): the redundancy tier's grain
and the persona's ask, with nothing the player set. Empty when the
contract asks for no spread. `requires_fault_isolation` and
`requirements_unmet_mask` bit 3 are judged at THIS grain, so the chip
names it; `spread_grain_in_force` may be stricter, and that is the
player's own promise. Msgpack-only, `Default` on the capnp decode
beside `spread_grain_in_force`.

cost_infrastructure_dollars.description:
The infrastructure half of `margin_cost_dollars` (`TenantCost::
infrastructure`), host share incl. facility.

cost_transit_dollars.description:
The transit half of `margin_cost_dollars` (`TenantCost::transit`),
upstream bytes. The one cost that arrives already per-customer.

cpu_load_pct.description:
Offered CPU as a percentage of what this tenant CONTRACTED, uncapped, so
it reads past 100 when they are asking for more than they rent.

This is the number that explains a latency spike on hosts that look idle.
A VM queues on its OWN vCPU ceiling, and the queue curve bites from
`queue_util_knee` (70%) upward: 25 ms at 95%, 168 ms at 99%, ~1990 ms at
the clamp. Host utilisation is a DIFFERENT quantity and does not move
with it, which is why a player checking the host map after a p99 spike
finds nothing wrong. 0 when the
tenant has no placed VMs.

distinct_hosts.description:
How many separate chassis this tenant's units are spread across, the
anti-affinity story. Its siblings `unit_count` and `max_units_on_host`
stay on the row because `services_view.gd` rolls them up fleet-wide;
this one has only the console.

egress_gbps.description:
Smoothed bandwidth attributed to this customer across their
service mix. Egress = response bodies / GET fan-out / etc.;
ingress = request bodies / PUT uploads / replication writes.
Real workloads are asymmetric (image hosting = egress-heavy;
backup ingest = ingress-heavy) and surfacing both reflects
that.

Their one fleet-wide reader was `network_view.gd`'s top-8 traffic
table, which now reads [`CustomersSummary::top_traffic`].

eviction_fee_dollars.description:
Termination fee (dollars) the operator would pay to evict this customer
right now, the tier's `eviction_penalty_frac` of one month's run-rate
(decoupled from the SLA-outage refund), plus any unused prepay on a
still-active Reserved contract (capped), clamped to current cash. Shown
on the Evict action so the player sees the bill before arming it.

failed_last_hour.description:
Failed requests since the last hourly snapshot, the delta the
inspector reads as "12 errors this hour." Reset by the engine
each hour boundary (`failed_at_hour_snapshot`).

fault_ask_grain.description:
**The LEVEL behind that bool**, mirroring
`ProspectView::fault_ask_grain` so the card a player reads before
signing and the row they read afterwards cannot drift. Empty tag = no
level stated.

fault_ask_max_share_pct.description: The share, 1..=100. Meaningless when `fault_ask_grain` is empty.

growth_ceiling_vms.description: Plateau, the max VM count this persona compounds to (0 = unknown/none).

kind_label.description:
Short-code service mix as ONE label, "fn" / "vm" / "obj" / "lb" /
"db" / "cdn", or the engine's join for a multi-service tenant. Byte for
byte identical to `CustomerView::archetype`, which is the field the
roster header reads; this one is the console's copy.

latency_top_term.description:
Pre-rendered dominant latency term, e.g. "queue 940.2 ms (94%)", or empty
when nothing has been sampled yet.

The engine already attributes latency across serve floor / fabric /
queue / CPU contention / attack / backbone / hairpin / cold start and
ranks them, but that breakdown only ever reached the INCIDENT card. The
customer panel is where a player asks "why is this tenant slow", so the
leading term belongs here too. Formatted render-side because the client
has no business re-deriving shares.

margin_cost_dollars.description:
Monthly cost honestly attributable to this tenant,
`GrossMargin::attributable_cost`. Their share of the hosts they occupy
(including those hosts' rack-U share of the facility) plus the upstream
transit bought for their bytes. Excludes overhead BY CONSTRUCTION; see
`CustomersSummary::overhead_dollars`.

margin_revenue_dollars.description:
Steady-state MONTHLY revenue for this tenant's live contract,
`GrossMargin::revenue`, i.e. `meter_projected` + `rate`, the same pair
that quotes a prospect. NOT an accumulator: pairing it with
`revenue_total_dollars` (lifetime) would compare two different months.

required_arch.description: Raw CPU-arch requirement tag ("x86_64"/"riscv"/…) or "" if agnostic.

required_region.description: Data-residency region the contract pins to, if any.

requirements_unmet_mask.description:
Bitmask of the customer's ASKED contract requirements that are currently
UNMET, so the always-on requirement chips render met (green) vs unmet
(amber) instead of alarm-amber for every ask. Stable wire bit layout:
bit 0 = multi-AZ, 1 = private-segment/dedicated, 2 = data-residency,
3 = fault-isolation (spread). Derived from `Engine::unmet_requirements`;
0 = every asked requirement is satisfied (or none is asked). A chip is
MET when its requirement is asked (the existing demand bools) and its bit
is clear.

**This field is exactly why the split is an `Option` and not 41 stripped
scalars.** Withheld, it would read `0`, "every requirement met", which
is not merely missing, it is the opposite of an alarm.

requires_fault_isolation.description:
True when the contract ASKS for fault isolation, copies of the tenant's
workloads kept off a shared fault domain (redundancy tier > 1 host
replica, or an archetype that requires anti-affinity). This is the ASK
side of `requirements_unmet_mask` bit 3; without it a client can render
the spread chip UNMET but never MET, because the mask alone cannot
distinguish "asked and satisfied" from "never asked". Mirrors
`ProspectView.requires_fault_isolation`.

revenue_total_dollars.description:
LIFETIME revenue billed to this tenant, dollars, an accumulator, not a
rate. Deliberately NOT paired with `margin_revenue_dollars`, which is a
monthly run rate; pairing them compares two different months.

Its one fleet-wide reader was `money_view.gd`'s top-10 table, which now
reads [`CustomersSummary::top_revenue_lifetime`], an EXACT ranking
folded once from the engine roster, in cents, with ties broken by id.

satisfaction.description:
Composite customer satisfaction in `0.0..=1.0`, folds health,
relationship trust, and long-term sentiment into one player-facing
"how's this relationship" number (see `CustomerState::satisfaction`).
The BAND is `CustomerView::satisfaction_label` and stays on the row.

serving_units.description:
SERVING ON SURVIVORS: how many units answered for this tenant on the
last serving sweep, and how many of those were not carrying a full
share, a box that is down, uncorded or off the fabric, or one behind a
front door the fleet has started steering traffic away from.

Losing a unit costs this tenant CAPACITY, not demand: the survivors pick
its requests up, and while they have the headroom the tenant reads
perfectly healthy on every other figure here. That is the intended
behaviour and it is also how a fleet ends up one failure from falling
over with nothing on screen saying so. `serving_units_degraded > 0` is
the statement that somebody else is carrying this tenant's work.

A RATIO, not a verdict: the client decides what to draw. Zero/zero is a
tenant with no serving units this sweep, which is not the same as a
healthy one and must not render as "fine".

Msgpack-only, `Default` on the capnp decode beside `contract_grain`.

sla_credits_dollars.description:
SLA-breach credits accumulated this billing period (issued back
to the customer; net negative for the provider). Lifetime sum.

sla_p99_budget_ms.description:
Latency-budget tier, milliseconds the customer's SLA tolerates
at p99. `None` for Bronze (no latency budget).

sla_period_availability_frac.description:
SLA accrual, billing-period model: the availability
fraction accrued THIS billing period (since
`CustomerState::sla_period_start`), `1 - failed/total` over
`sla_period_requests_{total, failed}`. Guards divide-by-zero: `1.0`
(nothing to fault yet) when no requests have accrued this period.
This is the EXACT figure `Engine::settle_sla_period` compares against
`SlaTier::availability_target()` at period close, distinct from
`CustomerView::availability_pct` (the recovering rolling EWMA read for
the health headline, not what the bill is judged on). Surfaced so a
credit on the bill is explainable instead of appearing from nowhere
(see `memory/billing_authority_design_2026_07_27.md`).

sla_period_elapsed_seconds.description:
Sim-seconds elapsed since this billing period started accruing
(`CustomerState::sla_period_start` to now), the denominator for
`sla_period_seconds_over_latency`, so the client can render "over
budget N% of the period" instead of a bare seconds count.

sla_period_seconds_over_latency.description:
Seconds accrued THIS billing period where the short-window p99
(`p99_recent_ms`) sat over the tier's `sla_p99_budget_ms`, mirrors
`CustomerState::sla_period_seconds_over_latency`. Always 0 for Bronze
(no latency budget, never accrues). Pair with
`sla_period_elapsed_seconds` to get the fraction
`SlaTier::latency_penalty_band` bands (2% / 10% / 30% thresholds).

spread_grain_in_force.description:
The grain this tenant is HELD TO right now (`Engine::spread_grain_in_force`
tag), empty when nothing holds them. `requires_fault_isolation` is true
for a tenant the PLAYER gave a grain as well as one whose persona asked,
so the Health tab's requirement row needs this to say "kept apart across
zones, your setting" instead of a bare "copies kept apart" over a promise
nobody but the player made.

CustomerFilterCounts.description:
Filter-pill counts paired with `CustomersSummary`. One field per
`_CUST_FILTER_*` id on the client. Engine semantics owned here, if
the filter logic changes (e.g. TOP becomes "top 10" instead of
"top 5"), this is the one place to update.

at_risk.description:
`_CUST_FILTER_AT_RISK`: same as `CustomersSummary.at_risk`,
surfaced again for symmetry so all four pill counts read from
one struct.

top.description:
`_CUST_FILTER_TOP`: `min(5, customers.len())`. The "top 5 by
recent revenue" list-cap mirrors the GDScript `_cust_filter_count`.

CustomerRankView.description:
One tenant's slot in [`CustomersSummary::top_revenue_lifetime`].

Id plus magnitude, never a name: `CustomerView::name` is on the row every
session already holds, so shipping it again would let a rank row and its
roster row disagree about what a tenant is called.

id.description: `CustomerView::id`. Join to the roster for the name, tier and mix.

revenue_total_cents.description:
Lifetime revenue in CENTS. Integer so the renderer's fingerprint gate
is exact, the same rule as `mrr_total_cents`.

CustomerRequestView.description:
A pending customer request, the
generalized "a customer wants something, your answer has consequences"
surface. Resolved via `PlayerCommand::ResolveCustomerRequest`.

accept_label.description:
Plain-words label for the accept action ("Provision for it" / "Match
the offer" / "Grant discount" / "Support it").

decline_label.description: Plain-words label for the decline action.

kind.description:
Request kind tag: "CapacitySurge" / "PoachThreat" / "CostConcession" /
"ComplianceRequest". Drives the card icon/colour.

summary.description:
Pre-rendered, player-facing one-liner ("we've got an event next week,
expecting ~10x traffic, can you stand up 4 more VMs?").

CustomerTrafficRankView.description:
One tenant's slot in [`CustomersSummary::top_traffic`]. Id plus both
directions, for the same join-don't-duplicate reason as
[`CustomerRankView`].

egress_kbps.description:
Smoothed egress in KILOBITS per second, the ranking key. Integer for
fingerprint exactness; the renderer divides by 1e6 once at format time
to get the Gbps it displays.

ingress_kbps.description:
Smoothed ingress in kilobits per second. Not a ranking key; carried so
the traffic row can draw both bars from one entry.

breached.description:
True while this tenant is in a BREACHED state, a sustained, unmitigated
intrusion compromised them. Drives the "BREACHED" risk pill; distinct from
(and more severe than) an availability incident.

oneOf.description:
**The drilldown half of a tenant.** The host withholds it from every
session that has not subscribed to this tenant (`Request::SubscribeCustomer`),
under the same gate as `services` and `service_margins`.

`None` means withheld. An `Option` is used because a zeroed scalar cannot
say it was withheld: `margin_dollars: 0.0` is a legal margin and
`requirements_unmet_mask: 0` means every requirement is met.
`detail_omitted` covers `services` and `service_margins`, which are
`Vec`s. One gate sets both, so `detail_omitted == detail.is_none()`.

`CustomerDetail::All` populates it, which is what the HTTP API's
`/api/v1/customers` route uses.

detail_omitted.description:
`true` when `services`, `service_margins` and [`CustomerView::detail`]
were WITHHELD from this session rather than being genuinely empty.

Same rule, and the same reason, as `ChannelView::is_preview`: a
reader that infers "this tenant has no services" from an empty vector
draws an empty console for a tenant with a full estate, and the failure
is silent. A customer really can have zero priced services, so the
vector's emptiness cannot carry this.

**It is not a second contract beside `detail`, it is the marker for the
two `Vec`s that cannot carry their own.** One gate sets all three, so
`detail_omitted == detail.is_none()` holds by construction and is
LINTED (`customer_detail_is_the_same_gate_as_detail_omitted`). A new
reader should test `detail`'s presence; this stays because it is a
published field with live readers.

in_latency_spike.description:
True when the customer is currently in a sustained latency
spike (engine edge-trigger). Drives an SLA-breach pill in the
inspector.

margin_dollars.description:
`margin_revenue_dollars - margin_cost_dollars`. GROSS margin. Negative
means the tenant loses money before a single dollar of payroll.

STAYS ON THE ROW while its two operands do not (they are on
[`CustomerDetailView`]): `customers_view.gd` appends it as an
engineering column for EVERY visible row under "More detail", so it is
a roster field that happens to be financial, not a drilldown one.

on_probation.description:
True when the customer is on probation, engine flag for
"they're seriously considering churn." The renderer can show
this with an at-risk pill.

p50_latency_ms.description:
Median (p50) request latency in milliseconds, the "typical"
number players read as "how's this customer doing", distinct from
the p99 tail. Float, so lightly-loaded customers don't all collapse
to the same whole-ms value. `None` until the window has samples.

p99_latency_ms.description:
p99 request latency over the LONG window (`CustomerState::latency`,
`tuning.latency_window_secs`: a rolling 5 game-minutes). REQUEST-WEIGHTED:
99% of the tenant's requests in the window were faster
than this, and a failed request counts at the request timeout, so this
reaches the timeout once more than 1% of the window's requests failed.
(It was the worst ~10 of 1000 per-sweep samples, ~4 game-hours.) This is
the SLA figure shown against `sla_p99_budget_ms`, stickier than
`p99_recent_ms` and never to be relabelled "now".

p99_recent_ms.description:
p99 request latency over the SHORT window (`CustomerState::latency_recent`,
`tuning.latency_recent_secs`: the last game-minute, request-weighted the
same way), cached by the engine once per metrics tick as
`CustomerState::recent_p99_ms`, which is also what the incident anomaly
machine opens and recovers on and what SLA latency money accrues against.

This is the "right now" number; the long window above holds a spike for
up to its 5 minutes after the tenant has recovered. Both ship so the
readout can be honest about which is which.

`None` until the first metrics tick after load (`load_reported` clears
the cached value because it describes a window that no longer exists).
Whole milliseconds, the engine caches it as `u64` ms and re-deriving it
here would mean a clone+sort of the window per customer per snapshot.

provisioned_total.description:
Units this tenant has PLACED, summed across every service class.

Always sent, whatever `detail_omitted` says. It is the roster's entire
need from `services` (`customers_view.gd` sums `provisioned_count` and
`requested_count` over the vector for its capacity-shortfall badge), so
shipping two integers lets the list keep working while the array it
walks stays behind the subscription.

requested_total.description:
Units this tenant CONTRACTED for, summed across every service class.
The other half of the roster's shortfall badge; see
`provisioned_total`.

rps.description:
Smoothed requests per second across this customer's workloads.
Mirrors `CustomerState.rps`. Drives the inspector's "Acme Co.
serves 4 req/s" plain-English read.

satisfaction_label.description:
Plain-words band for `satisfaction` (Delighted / Happy / Content /
Unsettled / At risk).

service_kinds.description:
Short-code service mix: subset of {"fn", "vm", "obj", "lb", "db",
"cdn", "k8s"} for the services this customer runs. Used by the
dashboard's Services drilldown to count tenants per service kind
and by the customer wall to render service-kind chips.

service_margins.description:
Per-service revenue/cost/margin split, `ServiceClass::ALL` order, zero
rows omitted (`GrossMargin::by_service`). Empty until the tenant has a
priced service.

services.description:
Per-service demand-vs-fulfilment breakdown, one entry per service
this customer is contracted for. Makes the gap between what a customer
asked for and what's actually live legible everywhere, instead of only
inferable from a health percentage. Reads `Engine::service_probe` for
state/reason so this view never re-derives feasibility/placement math.

**Populated only when this session asked for THIS customer's detail**
(`Request::SubscribeCustomer`), or for any reader that did not ask at
all, the HTTP API mirror, the TUI and tests all project at
`CustomerDetail::All`. A game session carries it for the tenant whose
console is open and nobody else. Read `detail_omitted`, never
`services.is_empty()`, to tell "not sent" from "has no services".

It is the expensive half of the section: `services` plus
`service_margins` is ~28% of the customers bytes, and the customers
section is 57.2% of a realistic baseline once the comms work landed.

stranded_unit_count.description:
Stranded VMs this customer owns, pinned to an unreachable
host with no auto-failover. Drives the red "N VMs stranded"
badge on the ops-console customer row and the comms-panel
incident card's `[Migrate]` quick-action.

threat_exposure_weight.description:
This tenant's contribution to the facility's AMBIENT exposure,
`archetype.threat.exposure_weight`, straight through.

**This is the number that answers "why is recon so high".** Ambient
threat is `floor + ln1p(Σ weight × fame)`, and
`threat_exposure_and_scale`'s own doc calls that sum "who, the
roster". A quiet tenant runs 0.1; a crypto exchange runs 2.0-3.0. It
lets a player watching their intrusion budget go amber learn that the
cause is who they have signed.

The BAND ("quiet / notable / high profile") is derived client-side by
one shared `OpsViewKit` call rather than shipped here: it is
presentation, and a `Text` field on every customer row is real bytes on
a section that rides every delta.

threat_targeted.description:
True when this archetype can be SINGLED OUT by a targeted attack,
`threat.attack_event_chance_per_month > 0`. A different lever from
`threat_exposure_weight`, which is the constant background hum: this
one is the monthly roll that launches a real composed attack at this
specific tenant.

Both belong on the prospect card, because they are different bargains.
A high-exposure tenant makes everyone noisier forever; a targetable one
is quiet until the day it is not.

under_attack.description:
True when a malicious attack is currently landing on THIS tenant, the
named victim of a targeted flood, or anyone the per-tenant impact pass is
failing requests for. Drives the "UNDER ATTACK" risk pill so the player
sees which tenant an attack is hurting, not just a fleet-wide board.

unit_count.description:
VM placement spread, the anti-affinity story made legible.
`vm_count` total VMs this customer runs; `vm_distinct_hosts` how
many separate chassis they're spread across; `vm_max_on_host` the
most this customer has on any single host (the worst-case "one
machine dies" blast radius). Anti-affinity raises distinct_hosts
and lowers max_on_host; bin-packing does the opposite.

CustomersSummary.description:
Customers-lens pre-computed counters + filter pill counts. Folded
from a single pass over the just-built `customers` Vec inside
`build_snapshot`, so the renderer's customers grid doesn't re-walk
the roster every 250 ms paint just to compute "ACTIVE / AT-RISK /
PROSPECTS / MRR EST." + the per-pill counts. Ships engine-authoritative
numbers, so GDScript and the engine cannot drift on filter semantics.

MRR is in **cents** (u64) instead of dollars (f64) so the renderer's
fingerprint-and-skip gate (`_cust_summary_fp`) is integer-exact,
float jitter at the cent boundary won't defeat the gate. Renderer
divides by 100.0 once at format time.

active.description:
All active customers (Active + Pending lifecycle). Equal to
`customers.len() as u32`, but pre-counted so the renderer's
summary band fingerprint is a single integer read.

at_risk.description:
Customers on probation OR currently in a sustained latency
spike: the "needs attention" count for the AT-RISK pill.

attributed_cost_dollars.description:
Sum of every tenant's `margin_cost_dollars` (`CostAttribution::
attributed`), monthly run rate.

filter_counts.description:
Per-filter counts mirroring the four customer-grid filter pill
ids in `ops_console_panel.gd` (`_CUST_FILTER_*`). Pre-computed so
the renderer's filter row fingerprint is the same single-pass
read as the summary band.

mean_availability_pct.description:
Fleet mean tenant availability, PERCENT, folded over every tenant in
`engine.customers`. `0.0` on an empty roster: ask `active > 0` rather
than reading `0.0` as an outage.

**A WORLD TOTAL MUST NOT BE PARAMETERISED BY WHICH CONSOLE IS OPEN.**
`availability_pct` sits on the customer TELEMETRY half, so
`record_to_delta` rotates it at `FAR_CUSTOMER_STRIDE = 32` (~8 s) for
every tenant EXCEPT `DetailScope::customer_detail`'s open one, which is
exempt and refreshes every tick. A client fold over those rows would
move when a tenant's console opens, so two sessions on the same world
at the same tick would read different fleet numbers. The fold is
therefore engine-side: exactly one source. Anything the roster CAN fold
at full freshness (`breached`, `service_kinds`) stays off this struct,
and `the_summary_does_not_duplicate_anything_the_roster_can_
still_derive` holds that line.

`f64` ON THE WIRE rather than the integer `mrr_total_cents` uses: this
struct already carries four `*_dollars` floats, the client's gate is
`changed("customers_summary")` rather than a value fingerprint, and
matching `CustomerView::availability_pct`'s own type and units avoids a
conversion. **The ACCUMULATOR behind it is an integer**:
`build_customers_summary` sums scaled `u64`s and divides once, because
float addition is not associative and this section is
content-addressed. Read that fold before changing either.

mrr_total_cents.description:
MRR estimate in cents: `sum(c.revenue_last_hour_dollars) × 24 × 30 × 100`.
Cents instead of dollars for integer fingerprint exactness.

overhead_dollars.description:
Monthly cost that is not attributable BY CONSTRUCTION: salary plus
debt service (`CostKind::is_overhead`). This MUST be rendered
outside every tenant's margin. "Gross margin" is only honest if the
unattributed remainder is visible next to it, and spreading payroll
across tenants by headcount or revenue share is an invented number.

service_last_hour.description:
Per-service last-hour revenue, one row per service kind the fleet
actually buys. Folded over every tenant at full freshness, for the same
reason as `mean_availability_pct`: `revenue_last_hour_dollars` is on
the customer telemetry half, so a client-side split would be a world
total the open console moves.

A `Vec` keyed by `ServiceConfig::kind_label` rather than one named
field per kind, so a new service kind adds a row and no field.

**The split is even.** The engine keeps no per-service revenue rate
(`RevenueBreakdownView` holds lifetime dollars and `service_margins`
holds margin), so a tenant's last-hour revenue is divided evenly across
the services they buy.

top_revenue_lifetime.description:
Tenants ranked by LIFETIME revenue, richest first, capped at
`TOP_REVENUE_K`. `revenue_total_dollars` lives on
[`CustomerDetailView`] and reaches no session that has not subscribed,
so the client cannot rank the roster itself.

**Aggregate exactly what the row does not carry, and nothing else.**
`customers_view.gd` states the counter-rule: "a count that is just a
list's length comes from that list, always", because a summary and an
array that could disagree eventually do. This ranking cannot be derived
client-side, so it is not a second source of truth; the breach count
and the availability mean `home_area.gd` folds from rows it holds are
deliberately NOT here.

EXACT, never sampled: folded once over `engine.customers.values()` in
`build_customers_summary`, in CENTS for the same integer-fingerprint
reason as `mrr_total_cents`, with **ties broken by ascending id** so the
order does not depend on hash-map iteration.

top_traffic.description:
Tenants ranked by smoothed EGRESS, heaviest first, capped at
`TOP_TRAFFIC_K`. `egress_gbps` / `ingress_gbps` are on
[`CustomerDetailView`], so the client cannot rank the roster itself.
Same exactness and tie-break rules as `top_revenue_lifetime`.

total_cost_dollars.description:
The fleet's whole monthly cost run rate. Invariant, exactly:
`attributed + unattributed + overhead == total`.

unattributed_cost_dollars.description:
Attributable-in-principle monthly cost that honestly reached NO tenant:
idle hosts, component/module depreciation, truncation residue
(`CostAttribution::unattributed_infrastructure`).

az_id.description:
AZ the box sits in, for EVERY location class including DeliveryZone.

A multi-building site has one staging zone per building, so a crate
waiting to be unpacked names the building it is waiting in, and the
client picks that building's pallet rather than whichever zone node it
finds first.

0 remains possible only on a save old enough to predate the field.

blocked.description:
Another box is stacked on top of this one, so it cannot be taken until
that one moves. Covers the pallet AND both hauler decks, so one flag
drives every take-off gate. The engine refuses a buried box outright
(`error-box-buried`); this is what lets the client grey it out of the
crosshair instead of offering a verb that will be refused.

capex_dollars.description: What capex was charged at order time (for the cancel refund preview).

content_depth_m.description:
Depth in metres of the boxed contents (server-deep vs switch-shallow).
Lets the client size the shipping box to its contents. Derived
from the SKU; `u_size` (above) drives box height.

content_width_class.description:
Footprint width class: "Full" (19" rack-width gear → wide box, both
trolley columns) vs "Small" (desktop/wall/tower → fits two-per-row).

held.description:
Is anybody carrying it? Separate from `held_by` because
`PlayerId::LOCAL` is `0`, so a box held by the HOST would otherwise
read as unheld to every other player.

held_by.description:
MULTIPLAYER, which player is carrying this box. Meaningless unless
`held` is true. The wire face of `PendingDelivery.held_by`.

The claim itself has existed engine-side since the co-op carry work
(`claim_delivery` / `delivery_spendable_by`), but it never reached the
wire, so it prevented corruption without preventing the BAD EXPERIENCE
it was written for: the other player's client kept drawing the box
sitting in the staging zone, because the only thing it could hide was
the box THIS client had picked up. They walked over, pressed E, and got
a bare "already carried" refusal about something their screen said was
there. The renderer had no way to know better.

Mirrors `CarriedItemView.owner`, which does the same job for entities.
Session state, not world state: `load_reported` clears the claim, so
this is always `0` on the first snapshot after a load.

is_existing.description:
True for "delivery" records that wrap an existing entity (created
by `unmount_from_rack`) rather than a fresh purchase. Renderer can
render these differently, e.g. the box is open and shows the held
item silhouette inside.

kind.description:
"Host" / "Switch" / "Appliance" / "PatchPanel", frontend uses this
to pick the right preview model and SKU lookup.

location.description:
Box location class: "DeliveryZone" / "Floor" / "Trolley". The
renderer dispatches off this, a Floor/Trolley box is drawn out in
the world at `position`; a DeliveryZone box uses the authored
staging-zone layout.

position.description:
World position when `location` is Floor/Trolley; [0, 0, 0] for
DeliveryZone (renderer ignores it there).

zone_pos.description:
Where the shipping-pallet packer put this box, in the delivery zone's
LOCAL space. `y` is the carton's BASE, not its centre, same
convention as `DeckPlacementView::pos`. All zeros when the box is not
on the pallet (carried, on the floor, or aboard a hauler).

The pallet packs through the same `sim_core::hauler::pack_deck` the
hauler decks use, so there is one stacking algorithm in the project
and the staging zone cannot disagree with the robot. The client does
not lay the zone out itself: a fixed grid with a constant layer step
floats short cartons and overlaps wide ones.

zone_yaw.description: Yaw in radians. Only ever 0 or a quarter turn.

DeviceTransitView.description:
Forwarding-derived per-device VNI transit, the REAL set of subnets (L2VNIs)
whose traffic transits a given forwarding device (switch / gateway /
appliance), so the switch/gateway/appliance consoles and the netview can show
"carrying {service} for {tenant}" from the actual forwarding path instead of
the first-hop guess.

Built in the projection from the SHARED forwarding graph
(`Engine::host_forwarding_device_path`): for every host carrying a subnet
(the inverse of `SubnetView.carrier_host_ids`), the ordered forwarding
devices on its path to the demarc each take that host's subnet ids; unioned
across hosts → this per-device set. `subnet_ids` (not parallel vrf/service
vecs) so each id joins back to its `SubnetView` for BOTH the service class
AND the tenant/VRF, preserving the pairing a flat pair of vecs would lose.

Msgpack keyframe-only (like `subnets` / `reservations` / `segments`), off
the per-tick capnp delta, no per-tick cost. `device_kind` is a plain string
("switch" / "gateway" / "appliance"), so no new wire enum. Empty until any
subnet is minted AND a carrier host's path resolves.

device_id.description:
Id of the device within its family (`SwitchId` / `GatewayId` /
`ApplianceId`, unique only together with `device_kind`).

subnet_ids.description:
The `SubnetView.id`s whose traffic transits this device. Sorted
ascending, deduped. Join each id to `WorldSnapshot.subnets` for the
service class + VRF (tenant) to render "carrying {service} for {tenant}".

EddStatus.description:
Health of one EDD, folded from its own uplinks. A figure the client cannot
derive at its own freshness belongs on the wire, populated from the
authority. The ladder is down beats saturated beats lit beats none, read
from the SAME per-line facts already on `UplinkView` (`failed`,
`saturated`) rather than a second computation; see `sim_project`'s
`EddView` populator.

chassis_depth_m.description:
Physical chassis depth in metres (mirrors `EddSku::chassis_depth_m`).
The renderer seats the mounted ears level with the rail plane from
this, 0 for wall-mount.

max_wan_port_gbps.description:
Fastest handoff-port speed (Gbps) this EDD exposes on its WAN side,
i.e. the ceiling on the uplink kinds it can carry (a 10 G line can't
land on a 1 G jack). The Internet panel filters its buy/upgrade lists
to kinds at or below this, so a site can't be offered lines it can't
physically support. 0 = no WAN ports.

port_count.description: Total physical port count exposed by this edd.

ports.description:
Per-port view (mirrors the host/switch convention). Lets the
rack-view popup look up port_id, peer, link state when the
player is routing a cable from a edd port.

power_feeds.description: Seated AC power cords (rear IEC inlets carrying a cord).

powered.description:
Whether the chassis is fed (≥1 AC cord, or wall-mount/cord-free). Drives
the MM dark-state gate (`multimesh_hardware` reads `powered`) and the
console, same as host/switch/gateway/appliance. `true` by default,
engine-booted EDDs auto-cord.

rack_id.description: Rack this edd is mounted in (0 = wall-mount / none).

sku_name.description:
SKU name (e.g. "1U Fibre Cross-Connect"). Port layout + media live on
`ports`.

start_u.description: Bottom U index in the rack (when rack-mounted).

status.description:
See [`EddStatus`]. Folded from `uplinks` below, never a client
threshold.

u_size.description: Rack U height consumed (0 for wall-mount).

used_ports.description: How many ports currently carry a switch cable.

wan_policy.description:
WAN uplink routing policy, "Failover" or "ActiveActive". Governs how
the carrier lines above share offered traffic (a policy, not a bond).
Drives the Internet-panel / gateway-console mode toggle.

EvidenceRowView.description:
One measured row on an incident card: what was measured, the value, and
the context that makes the value mean something (baseline, budget, share).

Deliberately pre-formatted engine-side. The numbers come with units,
precision and comparison baselines that only the engine knows, and every
client that re-derived them would drift; the renderer's job is layout.

detail.description:
Context that gives `value` meaning, "normal 88 ms · Gold budget
150 ms", or the full ranked breakdown. Rendered as a wrapping sub-line,
so unlike `value` it may be long. May be empty.

label.description: Row label, engineering voice, "p99 latency", "Where the time goes".

leading.description:
True when this row is the one that BREACHED (p99 over budget, the
dominant latency term, the leading failure cause), lets the client
weight it without re-deriving the engine's own verdict.

value.description:
The headline measurement, formatted with units, "412 ms", "6.2%".
Kept SHORT: the client renders it in a fixed-width, clipping column.

value_plain.description:
Plain-voice counterpart of `value`. Usually identical (a number is a
number); differs where the value names a term ("Queueing 4 ms" vs
"Waiting in line 4 ms").

This exists so `detail` never has to double as the plain-voice value.
It did briefly, and the result was both voices rendering at once in
both modes, with the jargon toggle merely reordering them, and, worse,
plain mode promoting the BASELINE into the headline slot so the
non-engineer saw "normal 88 ms" where the measured p99 belonged.

FinancingBreakdownView.description:
Cash IN that is neither revenue nor cost, projected from
`Engine::financing_breakdown`.

Exists so the Finance tab can explain a cash balance that revenue minus
cost does not account for. A quest payout is not business the player won,
and a bailout is a loan, so neither may read as revenue, but they moved
the cash, and a finance screen that cannot say where it came from is the
reason the reconciliation drift went unnoticed for so long.

bailout_injection_dollars.description:
Emergency-bailout principal. A LOAN: its repayments show up as
`service_debt` on the cost side.

total_financing_dollars.description:
Sum of the buckets above: `Engine::total_financing`, the third term of
`Δcash == Δrevenue - Δcost + Δfinancing`.

FloodProtectionView.description:
Carrier-side flood protection: plan state plus what this site is offered,
the static half of the Flood protection page (`sim_core::scrub`).
Keyframe-only, changes only on subscribe/cancel/relocate/line-purchase;
the live per-zone numbers ride `ActiveAttackView` instead (`edges`'
sibling `zones` carries the per-zone split).

active_plan.description:
The subscribed plan's catalog name (`ScrubPlan::name`), empty when no
plan is active.

active_since_ns.description: Sim-time the active plan was subscribed, 0 when none is active.

lines_gbps.description:
This site's live line capacity, summed across every zone
(`Engine::live_uplink_gbps`).

next_step_gbps.description:
The step after `protected_gbps`: what the contract re-sizes to once
the site's lines outgrow the current one. 0 with no lines.

offers.description:
What this site is OFFERED right now (`Engine::scrub_offers`): Proxy
only at a non-BGP site, Transit tiers only at a BGP-capable one.

protected_gbps.description:
The capacity a Transit contract is sized on: every bought line's
nameplate, whole site, rounded up to its step
(`Engine::scrub_protected_gbps`). 0 with no lines.

site_can_run_bgp.description:
Whether this site can physically terminate a line on a BGP-capable
gateway (`sim_core::scrub::site_can_run_bgp`), the availability gate
between the two products. Derived and stored on the engine, never
recomputed per tick.

FunctionPoolTenantView.description:
One tenant's slice of the Functions pool. Instances are per-tenant by
construction (`warm_slot` only reuses a container belonging to the same
customer at the same memory shape), so the pool total tells you nothing
about who is starved, this row does.

in_flight.description: This tenant's requests running at once, averaged over the last sweep.

oldest_queued_wait_ms.description:
Longest wait a served request of this tenant's paid in the last sweep,
ms: the cold start of a container booted for it. Zero when every
request found a warm slot.

queued.description:
This tenant's requests the last sweep turned away: no warm slot and no
room to boot a container. Each failed as `FunctionsSaturated`.

reserved_mem_mb.description: Memory this tenant's containers hold, MB.

saturated.description:
The engine's own verdict: no warm slot at this tenant's shape AND no
room to boot one. This is exactly the test behind
`ProbeReason::FunctionPoolSaturated`
(`Engine::function_pool_saturated`), not a re-derivation, so the panel
and the shortfall reason can never disagree.

FunctionPoolView.description:
The Functions warm pool, on the wire (`sim_core::pool::Fleet`).

The fleet has exactly one pool, so this is a keyframe-only section and not a
per-entity list. It holds scalars and a bounded per-tenant roster, with no
time series.

It carries the state behind the Functions saturation reason
(`ProbeReason::FunctionPoolSaturated`), failure term
(`FailureTerm::FunctionsSaturated`) and latency term
(`LatencyTerm::ColdStart`), so a reader can tell why requests queue.

Read it as three questions:
  * *Is work backing up?* `queue_depth` (requests the last sweep turned
    away) and `oldest_queued_wait_ms` (the cold start a served request
    waited out).
  * *Can the pool take another request without paying a cold start?*
    `free_slots` out of `slot_capacity`.
  * *If it has to boot, is there room?* `reserved_*` against `ceiling_*`.

booting_instances.description:
Subset of `instances` still inside their cold start (`ready_at > now`),
i.e. holding memory but not yet able to take new work.

ceiling_mem_mb.description:
Memory the pool may reserve up to, MB, fleet total minus what VMs hold
