(`Fleet::effective_total_mb`). This, not the raw fleet total, is
the number `can_boot` tests against.

ceiling_millivcpu.description:
CPU the pool may reserve up to, millivcpu
(`Fleet::effective_total_millivcpu`).

cold_start_ms.description: Policy: wall-clock penalty a request pays when it boots its container, ms.

cold_start_window_secs.description:
The window `cold_starts_recent` counts over, seconds. Shipped so the
label can be honest instead of assuming a constant.

cold_starts_recent.description:
Containers booted within the last `cold_start_window_secs`. Counted off
`FunctionInstance::booted_at`, so it needs no ring and no engine state;
exact as long as the window is shorter than the idle timeout (which
`cold_start_window_secs` is clamped to), because nothing that young can
have been reaped yet. Churn here is what puts `LatencyTerm::ColdStart`
in a tenant's p99.

concurrency_per_instance.description:
Policy (`FunctionExecPolicy`): requests one container serves at once
before another must boot. Without it, "12 in flight over 3 containers"
does not say whether you are at the ceiling.

free_slots.description:
Slots on READY instances with nothing in them, how many more requests
can land WITHOUT paying a cold start. Zero with headroom left = the next
request boots; zero with no headroom = saturation.

in_flight.description:
Requests running at once across every container, averaged over the
last sweep (Little's law: arrivals x duration / window). The sum of
the containers' `in_flight`.

instance_idle_timeout_secs.description: Policy: how long an idle container survives before teardown, seconds.

oldest_queued_wait_ms.description:
Longest wait any served request paid in the last sweep, ms: the cold
start of a container booted for it. Zero when every request found a
warm slot.

queue_depth.description:
Requests the last sweep turned away across every tenant: no warm slot
and no room to boot a container, each failed as `FunctionsSaturated`.
The headline number: non-zero means the pool is already behind.
(Functions are served once per sweep and nothing queues; the name is
kept for the wire.)

reserved_mem_mb.description:
Memory held by live containers, MB (`pool.used_mem_mb`). The reservation
is per-CONTAINER and lasts its whole life, not per-request.

reserved_millivcpu.description:
CPU held by live containers, millivcpu (`pool.used_millivcpu`).
Admission tests memory AND cpu; shipping only memory would make a
cpu-bound saturation read as "plenty of memory free, why is it
queueing?", exactly the invisible state this view exists to fix.

slot_capacity.description:
Concurrency slots on READY instances (`ready × concurrency_per_instance`).
Not derivable client-side from `instances`: booting containers are
excluded because they cannot take work yet.

tenants.description:
One row per tenant that has a live container, a queued invocation, or a
contracted Functions workload. Sorted by `customer_id` (the engine's
customer map is a `HashMap`, so the sort is what makes this
deterministic). Bounded by the Functions tenant count.

GatewayAddonView.description:
One fit-able gateway security add-on (archetype B, no box, throttles the
gateway). Static option data + this gateway's enabled state.

owned.description:
Capex already paid for this add-on on THIS gateway (the ownership
ledger). `enabled` add-ons are always owned; an owned-but-disabled
add-on can be RE-subscribed for free. Lets the console show
`Buy $X` → `Unsubscribe` → `Resubscribe (free)`.

GatewayView.description:
Live edge-gateway projection. WAN port(s) cable to the edd; LAN ports
to switches. Forwarding device in the reachability chain.

addon_throttle.description:
`forwarding_ceiling_gbps / fabric_capacity_gbps`, the fraction of rated
fabric the effective ceiling leaves, for the console's "×0.80" hint. 1.0
when nothing is throttling. A PRESENTATION of the ceiling below, derived
from it, so the two can never disagree; it is not an authored constant.

addon_throttled.description:
A gateway has NO deep-inspection engine. These three fields describe the
gateway's FORWARDING ceiling being reduced by the security add-ons fitted
to it, and nothing more. An add-on riding a router costs the router's ASIC
headroom; that penalty is a throttle on forwarding, not an inspection
throughput rating. Only a dedicated appliance has a real inspection plane
(`ApplianceView::inspection_*`), and a gateway must never read as capable
as one.

True when this gateway has a DPI add-on fitted (Σ deep-inspection
`inspection_capacity_gbps` > 0), i.e. something on the router is actually
costing it forwarding headroom.

NOT "some fitted add-on carries a `gateway_throttle`". The stateful
firewall add-on carries one but does no per-packet DPI, so the engine
charges it nothing; a firewall-only gateway reports `false` and keeps its
full rated ceiling below.

bgp_advertising.description:
Whether this gateway is CURRENTLY advertising the provider prefix, a
live, `bgp_capable`, internet-facing edge. Two or more advertising edges
= an HA border; a lone advertiser (or a non-BGP edge) is a border SPOF.

bgp_capable.description:
Whether this gateway's SKU can run BGP (eBGP to the carrier + HA
pairing). Entry/SOHO routers are single boxes, circuit redundancy only,
no router HA. Gates the "form a redundant pair" affordance.

builtin_firewall_enabled.description:
Whether the built-in firewall is switched ON. Player-toggleable from the
gateway console (→ `SetGatewayFirewall`); off removes this gateway's
Protocol baseline. Defaults true.

egress_gbps.description: Smoothed directional egress (LAN-side outbound) in Gbps.

fabric_capacity_gbps.description:
SKU fabric/forwarding ceiling, sustained traffic above this
saturates the ARM-ASIC packet engine. Legacy name kept as alias.

fabric_load_gbps.description:
Smoothed full-duplex fabric load in Gbps (= egress + ingress).
Compared against `fabric_capacity_gbps` for the saturation banner.

fabric_saturated.description:
True when sustained `fabric_load_gbps` exceeds `fabric_capacity_gbps`,
packets start dropping. Edge-triggered in the engine; banner
state here.

fabric_utilisation.description:
`fabric_load_gbps / forwarding_ceiling_gbps`. NOT `addon_throttle` (that is the ceiling's OWN
fraction of the nameplate; this is the LOAD against that ceiling).
Folded ONCE in the projection from the same two figures above, so the
forwarding meter's fill fraction and `fabric_saturated` cannot
disagree. `[0, 1+]`, not clamped. 0 when `forwarding_ceiling_gbps` is
0.

forwarding_ceiling_gbps.description:
The gateway's effective forwarding ceiling with its add-ons fitted.
`fabric_load_gbps` is the load against it, and it is the threshold
`fabric_saturated` flips on.

It depends on load: deep packet inspection eats forwarding headroom as
it engages, so this falls from the full fabric rating toward the
inspection ceiling as `fabric_load_gbps` rises. Read it from this field
and do not recompute it.

The `*_capacity_gbps` suffix is reserved for fixed integer nameplate
ratings, so this load-dependent value uses a different name.

indicator.description:
Status lamp, four-corner parity with Host / Switch / Appliance,
which all already carry one. `Off` while unpowered; `Red` on any
installed-part fault (`ComponentStatus::Failed`); otherwise the
kind's existing health arms.

ingress_gbps.description: Smoothed directional ingress (WAN-side inbound) in Gbps.

inv_status.description:
Lifecycle status, see `HostView::inv_status`. Four-corner parity with
Host / Switch / PatchPanel.

lan_port_count.description: Live count of ports currently cabled to a switch, i.e. acting LAN.

monthly_opex_dollars.description:
Live projected monthly opex ($/mo), running fee + chassis power +
seated-optic draw. Mirrors the host console's read.

multi_az_capable.description: Whether the SKU can be a multi-AZ region border (implies `bgp_capable`).

power_feeds.description:
Connected AC cord count. >= 2 = PSU-failure resilience at
`redundant_psu_overhead_w` extra draw per extra cord.

powered.description:
At least one AC cord seated (or none required). False = dark
until the player plugs it in. Mirrors the engine's `powered`.

psu_dark.description:
True when no corded PSU can deliver power: every lamp reads dark,
`indicator` forced `Off` alongside it. See `HostVisual.psu_dark`.

security_addons.description:
One row per available gateway security add-on (advanced firewall /
basic IPS / basic scrub). `enabled` reflects whether THIS gateway has
it fitted. The console renders a CheckButton per row with capex+monthly
+ the throttle warning, dispatching `SetGatewayAddon`.

threats.description:
Per-class threat rows for THIS gateway, one row per class reaching it,
defended or not. Defended classes are the built-in L3/L4 firewall's
(Protocol / Volumetric / Intrusion) plus any enabled add-on's (Intrusion
via Basic IPS, Volumetric via Basic Scrub); undefended classes (L7
Application, or anything whose defence is switched off) still appear at
`mitigated: 0, capacity: 0` with `defense_capable` telling them apart.
Same shape + shared `ThreatMitigationView` as `ApplianceView::threats`,
so the gateway console renders the identical per-class Threats
breakdown the appliance does. The built-in firewall's Protocol share is
the row with `class == "protocol"`. Empty only when the gateway is off
the internet path entirely.

wan_policy.description:
This router's WAN uplink policy across ITS circuits ("Failover" /
"ActiveActive"). The console's WAN tab toggles it. The router, not the
passive EDD, owns the routing decision.

wan_port_count.description:
Live count of this gateway's ports currently cabled to the carrier
(a edd / patch panel), i.e. acting WAN. Derived from cabling,
not a nameplate: gateways are ARM-ASIC and have no fixed WAN ports.

additional_ssd_gb.description:
**Disk (GB) the ask demands**, the dimension an object-store or
database ask is actually about. `0` on an ask that consumes no disk, and
`#[serde(default)]` yields `0` for a payload that omits it.

additional_ssd_iops.description:
**Disk IOPS the ask demands.** The other half of a storage ask: two
tenants can want the same gigabytes and place very differently. Same
`#[serde(default)]` contract as
[`Self::additional_ssd_gb`].

additional_units.description:
How much more, in that class's own units. See [`Self::class_tag`], this
is NOT a VM count except when `class_tag` is "vm"; the field name is
kept for wire compatibility.

additional_vcpu_milli.description:
vCPU (milli) the ask demands.

**This is the ask's footprint in ONE dimension of six, and which
dimension matters depends on `class_tag`.** The engine computes a full
`Footprint` (mvcpu, mem, ssd GB, ssd IOPS, vGPU slices, GPU mem) for
every ask. An object-store tenant asking for "+1 GB of storage" would
read "+0.6 vCPU, +1.1 GB RAM" here and nothing at all about storage.
Read the dimension that matches the class, not this one by default.

class_tag.description:
**Which service is being asked for more of**, `ServiceClass::tag()`
("vm", "k8s", "obj", "cdn", "db", "fn", "lb").

The client selects the noun off this in Fluent (`-growth-unit`), so a
Kubernetes tenant reads "+2 workers" and an object-store tenant reads
"+500 GB of storage" rather than "+N VMs".
`#[serde(default)]` yields "vm", the class of an ask that carries no tag.

customer_name.description: Resolved customer name, from the customer record.

fit_can_serve_now.description:
True when the fleet can absorb the ask at 1:1 right now (fits within
physical headroom, low contention). No new hardware needed.

fit_oversubscribed.description:
True when approving would push the fleet PAST physical into overcommit:
it still fits under the host overcommit ceiling, but CPU is shared and
tenants may slow under load. Never a false "can't fit".

fit_recommendation.description:
Contention-tier one-liner: "Comfortable" / "Tight fit" / "Will run
oversubscribed (CPU shared under load)" / "Over capacity, add hardware
first" / "No VM load".

fit_vcpu_after_pct.description:
Projected fleet vCPU utilization after this ask's additional VMs land
(physical basis, display-only). 0.0 when the customer runs no VM demand.

resize_add_memory_mb.description: RAM (MB) to add to EACH existing VM's spec. See [`Self::resize_add_vcpu`].

resize_add_vcpu.description:
**A VERTICAL ask**: vCPU to add to EACH existing VM's spec, `0` when the
customer is only asking for more VMs.

Without these the client cannot tell a resize ask from a count ask, and
a pure resize (`additional_units == 0`) would render as "+0 VMs", a
request to change nothing. These carry the engine's `spec_resize`.

segment_dedicated_hosts.description:
Dedicated host count in that segment (dark hosts included); 0 when
shared-fleet.

segment_free_vcpu_milli.description:
Free/total capacity of the serviceable hosts this customer's ask can
land on (the set the fit verdict judged), whether or not the customer
sits on a dedicated segment.

segment_name.description:
Customer's isolation segment name when pinned to an L3VNI backed by
dedicated hosts (fit is scoped to it). "" for shared-fleet tenants.

segment_vni.description: L3VNI of that dedicated segment; 0 when shared-fleet.

traits.description: Personality trait names surfaced in the draft. Empty for none.

HostPoolView.description:
A player-created host pool. Small top-level list on `WorldSnapshot`
(msgpack-only, like `lags`); per-host membership rides `HostView.pool_id`.
`serves` are `ServiceClass` tags ("vm"/"fn"/"obj"/"db"/"cdn"/"k8s").

host_count.description:
Count of hosts currently assigned to this pool, saves the client a
scan when rendering the pool list.

age_hours.description: Wall-clock age in hours since first install.

allocated_millivcpu.description:
Sum of vCPU (in millicores) *allocated* to placed VMs on this host
(`Host::committed_millivcpu`). This is the promised/reserved figure,
not the live demand, compare against `physical_vcpu * 1000` to show
the oversubscription fill.

carried_by.description:
Whose hands, as a seat id, or 0 when nobody is holding it.

READ IT WITH `inv_status`, never alone: 0 means "not carried" only
because the pair is read together. Its job is to make
`Carried { player }` expressible on the entity's OWN row, so a renderer
can resolve where a device is, rack, hands, floor, from one field set
that rides the normal per-tick path.

The separate `carried_items` section is keyframe-only, content-hashed,
and emitted exactly once when it empties; a client that missed that
single frame would believe it still held a racked device, so this row
is the authority for the local player.

EXISTENCE AND LOCATION ARE NOT SCOPABLE. This field is top-level and
always present; it must never move behind a detail/LoD gate, or a
device whose detail you are not owed renders in the wrong place, or
nowhere.

contention_state.description:
Contention read-out: `"healthy"` (demand well under effective capacity),
`"warm"` (demand > ~0.8× effective), `"contended"` (demand exceeds
effective capacity, VMs are being throttled). Drives the host console's
green/amber/red contention indicator.

display_name.description:
Player-facing identity like `srv-01`. Unique per host; survives
SKU upgrades and moves. Prefer this over `sku_name` when labelling
the host in UI: `sku_name` is the model designation, shared
across many hosts.

display_name_plain.description:
Plain-mode counterpart: `server 1` vs `srv-01`. Two-voice per
`[[two_voice_labels_2026]]`. Empty on legacy saves; clients should
fall back to `display_name`.

effective_nic_gbps.description:
The line rate this host can ACTUALLY push (Gbps): the LAG
aggregate when its NICs are bonded, else the forwarding link's
negotiated rate, else the SKU nameplate when unwired. Same figure and
same meaning as `HostConsoleSnapshot::effective_nic_gbps` (the
focused-host twin), folded here so a fleet-wide reader (the Network
page's busiest-hosts ranking) has a real per-host denominator.

0 on the first tick after a load, before the engine's metrics sweep has
run once (`Engine::traffic.host_effective_nic_gbps` is rebuilt on the first
sweep, `#[serde(skip)]`, never persisted). A CLIENT MUST NEVER DIVIDE
BY THIS RAW: treat 0 as "not yet known" and fall back to the SKU
nameplate rather than producing NaN or an infinite share.

egress_gbps.description:
Smoothed network egress in Gbps for this host's link cable.
Accumulated across the customer's full service mix on this
host (Functions, VMs, ManagedDb, ObjectStore, LB, CDN, K8s).
Drives per-port throughput at the cable's host-end + the
switch port the cable lands on.

free_mem_mb.description:
Absolute free memory in MB (`Host::free_mb()`). Same accessor as the
`migrate_vm` capacity gate.

free_ssd_gb.description:
Absolute free SSD in GB (`Host::free_ssd_gb()`). Same accessor as the
`migrate_vm` capacity gate.

free_vcpu_milli.description:
Absolute free vCPU in millicores (`Host::free_millivcpu()`), i.e.
effective capacity minus VM + service-reserved usage. Mirrors the
exact accessor `migrate_vm` gates on, so the migration picker can
offer only hosts a specific VM footprint actually fits.

gpu_mem_mb_total.description:
Total GPU frame-buffer (MB) across all physical GPUs
(`HostSku::total_vgpu().1`). 0 for a non-GPU host.

ingress_gbps.description:
Smoothed ingress (data flowing IN, request bodies, PUT
uploads). Surfaced separately so the inspector can show
asymmetric flows ("↑ heavy / ↓ light") accurately.

inv_status.description:
WHERE THIS DEVICE IS: `"Mounted"`, `"Carried"` or `"Loose"`. The
canonical `inv_status` doc; every other view's points here.

THIS FIELD IS THE LOCATION, and rendering is a total function of it.
`rack_id` / `start_u` are NOT location: a device keeps them as a
historical hint after it leaves a rack, so a renderer that reads them
alone keeps drawing a machine that is in somebody's hands. Read this
first, and pair it with `carried_by`, 0 means "nobody" only because the
two are read together, since 0 is also a valid seat.

A `Loose` device's POSITION is not here: it rides `loose_items`.
Location comes from this field, position from there, and a
`loose_items` row is only honoured when the two agree; see
`IpcClient.loose_items_confirmed`.

link_capacity_gbps.description:
Modal NEGOTIATED link capacity among the `link_count` cabled ports, ties
broken toward the FASTER speed. 0 when nothing is patched.

Same quantity and same name as `PortView::link_capacity_gbps`, one level
up, never a SKU nameplate. `SwitchView::port_capacity_gbps` is the
nameplate and reads differently on purpose: a 32x400G spine with one 25G
patch lead has `port_capacity_gbps == 400` and `link_capacity_gbps == 25`.

link_count.description:
Cabled data ports on this device: ALWAYS present, whatever `ports` did.

Exactly `_connected_port_summary`'s predicate: `link_capacity_gbps > 0`
(which excludes the capacity-0 IEC power inlets the engine mints above
the data ports) AND a non-empty `cable_ids`. Derived from the same
`Vec<PortView>` in one helper (`cables::summarize_ports`) so the summary
and the array can never disagree.

link_mixed.description:
More than one distinct negotiated speed among the cabled ports, so a
label can say "25G+" instead of claiming every link runs at the mode.

mem_requested_pct.description:
REQUESTED (reserved/committed) share, NOT live usage: numerator is
`vm_used_* + service_reserved_*`, denominator NAMEPLATE `sku.*`. Live
demand rides `used_millivcpu` on this same struct, the two answer
different questions, hence the explicit `requested` in the name.

model_sku.description:
The base SKU whose model renders this one: a content-pack SKU borrows
a built-in chassis. Empty means `sku_name` itself.

mtbf_hours.description:
SKU MTBF in hours, so the inspector can show "120k
expected, 18k used" without re-resolving the catalog.

nic_count.description:
Physical NIC port count. T1-T2 SKUs are single-NIC; T3+ ship
multi-NIC for LACP redundancy. Defaulted via serde.

nic_module_slots.description:
Rear cages that accept a purchasable SFP NIC module
(`HostSku.module_slots`). 0 = the chassis takes no modules.

nic_modules_installed.description:
NIC modules currently installed (`Host.nic_modules.len()`), bounded
by `nic_module_slots`.

online.description:
Whether the host is up on the network right now: powered on AND
reachable through a live uplink chain (engine `host_is_serviceable`).
The honest "online/offline" signal: a host that's cabled but whose
uplink chain is down reads `false`, unlike a naive "any cable attached"
check. Defaulted via serde for old / partial payloads.

overcommit_max.description:
Hard ceiling on `overcommit_target` (`config.tuning.vcpu_overcommit_max`).
Clamps the player-facing slider.

overcommit_target.description:
Player-dialed overcommit target for this host (`Host::overcommit_target`).
`1.0` = strictly 1:1 (dedicated); higher permits oversubscription up to
`overcommit_max`.

physical_vcpu.description:
Physical vCPU count exposed by this host's SKU (`HostSku::vcpu`).
The denominator for the overcommit ratio; `allocated_millivcpu`
may exceed `physical_vcpu * 1000` when the host is oversubscribed.

ports.description:
Per-NIC readouts, same content as `RackInspectSnapshot`'s host
occupant ports, so the workbench inspector can show speed / state /
activity per NIC. Populated for every host this session is scoped for;
`apply_port_detail` withholds it for the rest.

SCOPABLE DETAIL.
`None` = "this session was not sent this device's ports", NOT "this
device has none": a portless device is a real state and it says
`Some([])`. The two must stay distinguishable, or truncation reads as
deletion. The client's marker is key
PRESENCE (`view.has("ports")`, `netview_canvas._port_summary_for`), which
is why this is `skip_serializing_if` rather than an empty vec, and why
`HostViewCp` carries a companion `portsPresent` bool, capnp decodes an
unset list as an EMPTY list and would otherwise erase the distinction at
the encoding layer.

`link_count` / `link_capacity_gbps` / `link_mixed` below are ALWAYS populated
from this same array, so every fleet-wide reader keeps a true answer
when the array itself is withheld.

Withheld only by `ViewportFilter::DetailBounded` (`apply_port_detail`).

power_feeds.description:
Connected AC cord count (0..=psu_count). >= 2 = PSU-failure
resilience at `redundant_psu_overhead_w` extra draw per extra cord.

powered.description:
At least one AC cord seated (or none required, wall rack,
unracked, or cord-free scenario). False = the box is dark until
the player plugs it in. Mirrors engine `Host.powered`.

resale_dollars.description:
Resale value at current condition + age. Same value the engine
credits if the item is sold right now.

served_customer_ids.description:
Customers whose workload currently has presence on this host,
VM allocations, in-flight Function invocations, ManagedDb
primaries, K8s nodes. Sourced from engine allocation maps; the
inspector filters its tenant list to this set when scoped to a
single host. Order: customer id ascending (deterministic).

service_classes.description:
Service-class tags this host serves a data-plane agent for (service
plane). Lets the Services page list a service's allocated hosts exactly
rather than approximating via served-customer overlap. Empty when the
model is off. Small (0-3 tags); changes rarely.

start_u.description: Starting U slot inside the rack.

stranded_unit_count.description:
Stranded units still pinned to this host: allocations whose customer is
`Single` tier and whose host has lost reachability while remaining
powered up. Drives the diegetic inspector's "N stranded" line. 0 when
nothing is stranded on this host.

Generic over service class: a stranded shard, worker or POP counts here
too.

unit_count.description:
Every placed unit on this host, across all seven service classes.
Includes stranded units, whose last known host is still the only place
they claim. [`HostView::stranded_unit_count`] is that subset, so
`unit_count - stranded_unit_count` is what is actually running.

This is the only per-host workload count. A count of VMs alone reads 0
for a host that carries only CDN POPs, Kubernetes workers, LB proxies,
object shards or function containers.

used_millivcpu.description:
Live vCPU *demand* in millicores (`Host::used_millivcpu_total`),
i.e. what the workloads are actually asking for this tick. Compared
against `eff_millivcpu` (physical × overcommit_target) to derive the
contention state.

vgpu_slices_total.description:
Total vGPU slices this host's SKU exposes across all its physical
GPUs (`HostSku::total_vgpu().0`). 0 for a non-GPU host. Pairs with
`vgpu_slices_used` for the inspector's GPU partition gauge.

vgpu_slices_used.description: vGPU slices currently reserved by placed VMs (`Host.vgpu_slices_used`).

wear_factor.description:
Wear multiplier on nameplate capacity (`eff_millivcpu = sku.vcpu *
wear_factor`). Without it a client reading this streamed view CANNOT
compute the wear-adjusted EFFECTIVE basis: it has nameplate and nothing
else. 1.0 = pristine.

accelerator_glow.description: 0.0..1.0, frontend uses for soft-glow on accelerator cards.

fault.description:
Any installed part (PSU / disk / fan / DIMM / CPU) is
`ComponentStatus::Failed`. `Degraded` does not set this: only a
Failed part is a "problem" for lamp purposes. Drives the front power
lamp red (solid) while the box still has power, and the PSU squares'
flash-red while at least one cord is fed. Single source of truth:
`sim_project::parts_fault_map`.

psu_dark.description:
True when no corded PSU can deliver power (every PSU Failed, or every
CORDED inlet's PSU Failed): the box reads exactly as dark as an
uncorded one, `status`/`indicator`/`fan`/`port`/`accelerator_glow` all
forced dark alongside it, though `fault` and `psu_failed` still carry
the reason for a console to explain. Single
source of truth: `sim_project::derive_host_visual`.

psu_failed.description:
Bitmask over PSU part slot (0-based `Component.slot`), bit `k` set
when PSU slot `k` is `ComponentStatus::Failed`. Slot `k` sits behind
inlet ordinal `k + 1` (`sim_core::component::inlet_for_psu_slot`), so
bit `k` is the `(k+1)`-th IEC inlet's own lamp: solid red regardless
of whether that inlet is corded, because the lamp belongs to the
PSU, not the cord.

HostilityView.description:
The world-hostility (danger axis) setting in force. See
`WorldSnapshot::hostility` for why this is a struct rather than a bare
`Option<f64>`.

The two fields answer different questions and both are needed: the settings
panel's segment has a "Match difficulty" option AND explicit levels, so it
must distinguish "following, and the effective multiplier happens to be 1.0"
from "explicitly pinned at 1.0". Collapsing them would make the segment
jump to the wrong option whenever difficulty sat at Standard.

follows_difficulty.description:
True when no override is set and hostility tracks difficulty. This is
the state `Engine::hostility == None` represents.

value.description:
The multiplier ACTUALLY in force, the override when one is set, and
difficulty's own multiplier when it is not. Always a real number, so a
readout never has to compute it and the two cannot disagree.

IncidentPartsView.description:
See `IncidentView::parts`. Buckets are mutually exclusive per part
(repairing > arrived > ordered), so `ordered + arrived + repairing <=
failed` always holds.

arrived.description: Failed parts with a replacement arrived, awaiting the swap.

failed.description: Currently-`Failed` parts on the incident's owner.

next_arrival_ns.description:
Earliest arrival (sim-time ns) among the `ordered` parts' orders.
`0` when nothing is on order.

ordered.description: Failed parts with a replacement on order, not yet arrived.

repairing.description: Failed parts with an open `SwapPart` work order.

detail.description:
Free-form details for variants that carry a payload (customer
name, work-order id, factor description). Empty for variants
that are pure transitions.

IncidentView.description:
Renderer-friendly mirror of `sim_core::incident::Incident`.
Channel UI, post-mortem, and the "is this customer impacted?"
badge all read from these. Severity (`EventView.severity`) is a
per-event tag; `band` here is the incident-level gravity read.

affected_customer_ids.description: Sorted ascending by id. Engine guarantees deterministic order.

affected_host_ids.description:
The MACHINES this incident is about, sorted ascending, capped at
`sim_core::incident::AFFECTED_HOSTS_CAP`. Empty for roots with no host
scope (DDoS, uplink saturation, customer-observation): those degrade
everyone, so naming hosts would be a lie. Resolve names against
`hosts[].display_name`.

affected_host_total.description:
True count before the cap, so the UI can say "showing 64 of 812"
rather than silently truncating.

article_ids.description:
Ids of the knowledge-base articles covering this root's mechanic, for
`open_codex:<id>` deep links. The client resolves the titles from the
`article-<id>-title` catalog key. May be empty.

az_id.description:
The zone this incident is rooted on: `AzOutage` and `Ddos` (a flood
lands on one zone's edge). 0 for every other root.

band.description:
Computed gravity band, "cosmetic" / "annoying" / "serious" / "existential",
weighed over the harmed tenants: duration alone never raises it past
"annoying" while nobody is harmed.

causes.description:
Ranked candidate causes, best-first, WITHOUT the lead cause when the
lead is the root itself (confirmed, live, confidence 100). That lead is
fully described by the `root_*` fields, `rack_id` and `article_ids`, so
a reader rebuilds it from them whenever `causes[0]` does not name
`root_kind` + `root_entity_id`.

channel_thread_id.description:
Channel thread root in `#incidents`. Populated once the channel
module lands (Pass A3); 0 until then.

compliance_at_risk.description: Worst compliance tier among the harmed tenants: a dash placeholder / "SOC2" / "HIPAA" / "PCI".

confirmed.description: True if any candidate cause has been confirmed as the real cause.

evidence.description:
MEASURED evidence behind a customer-facing symptom: the tenant's p99
against its own baseline and tier budget, its failure rate, where the
latency actually went, and why requests failed.

The card's guidance says "check their p99 latency vs tier budget", and
these rows are that figure. Empty for
infrastructure-rooted incidents with no tenant to measure.

hint.description: The current-tier escalating hint text (empty when `hint_tier == 0`).

hint_tier.description:
Highest progressive-hint tier fired for this incident (0 = none,
1 = subsystem nudge, 2 = named suspect, 3 = named fix).

max_sla_tier.description: Worst SLA tier among the harmed tenants, "Bronze" / "Silver" / "Gold" / "Platinum".

parts.description:
Parts-loop rollup for a `ComponentFailed`-rooted incident, how many
of the owner's failed parts are ordered / arrived-awaiting-repair /
mid-swap, and when the next ordered one lands. Zeroed for every
other root. Filled once per incident per keyframe rebuild in
`sim-project/src/incidents.rs::build_incident_parts`, never per
device per tick.

rack_id.description:
Rack the incident beacon should mark, resolved engine-side from the
typed root (device's rack, or the rack itself, or the edge rack where
WAN ingress lands for global/fabric roots). 0 when nothing is racked
yet. Lets the renderer skip a per-tick scan of every device array.

resolved_at_ns.description: 0 while open; set to the resolution sim-time once closed.

revenue_at_risk_per_hour_dollars.description:
Hourly run-rate of the tenants the incident HARMED. A tenant in
`affected_customer_ids` whose workload failed over cleanly adds nothing.

root_entity_id.description:
Primary entity id from the root, when there is one (host id,
cable id, rack id, ...). 0 for global roots like NetworkLoop; the
zone id for the zone-rooted `AzOutage` and `Ddos`.

root_msg_args.description: Facts for `root_msg_key`, including any already-resolved customer name.

root_msg_key.description:
Localization key for the root label, `incident-<root_kind-kebab>`.

Guidance ("what to check") deliberately has NO key field: it is static
per root and the client derives `guidance-<root_kind>-check-<n>` from
`root_kind`, which is already on this struct.

symptom_customer_id.description: Tenant the symptom is rooted on, or 0 for an `InfrastructureFault`.

symptom_kind.description:
Symptom layer, the customer/operator-facing HEADLINE the card leads
with (many causes → one symptom). Variant tag mirroring `Symptom`:
"ServiceUnreachable", "InfrastructureFault", etc.

symptom_msg_args.description:
Facts for `symptom_msg_key`. Empty when they are the same facts as
`root_msg_args`; a reader then resolves the symptom with `root_msg_args`.

symptom_msg_key.description: Localization key for the symptom headline, `symptom-<kind-kebab>`.

timeline.description:
Incident timeline, oldest first. Bounded only by incident
lifetime, preserved into the resolved-ring.

work_order_ids.description:
Active work order ids targeting this incident. Populated once
the work model lands (Pass A2); empty until then.

min_active.description:
LACP `min-links` semantic, the engine reports this so the
renderer's SpinBox can default to the current value when the
inspector opens.

price_multipliers.description:
Capex multipliers per host-shape category. The buy panel reads
this when stamping shop prices.

MigrationStatusView.description:
Live status of an in-progress relocation migration window, drives the HUD
countdown bar while carried tenants re-home on the fresh floor after a move.
`active` is false outside a migration (client hides the widget); it also
flips false early once every tenant is back Active.

seconds_left.description: Seconds left in the window (0 once elapsed).

site_display_name.description: Display name of the site being migrated into.

tenants_remaining.description: Tenants still re-homing (parked in the migration grace).

window_seconds.description: Full window length in seconds, the denominator for the bar fraction.

ModApiVersion.description: The version envelope every snapshot carries.

generation.description:
The API generation, as the manifest spells it (`"v1alpha1"`). A mod whose
manifest names another generation is refused at load.

minor.description:
The schema minor within the generation. A mod built against minor M reads
any snapshot of a later minor until one declares a break on a surface it
uses; from then on the loader refuses it ([`crate::api_support`]).

ModSnapshot.description:
What a script mod reads about the world at one quantum.

Each section is the `WorldSnapshot` field of the same name; see that
field's documentation for its meaning. `port_flows` is the per-port
throughput `/api/v1/network/port-throughput` serves. `workloads` is
every workload a migrate command can move, with the ids it takes.
`parts` is every device with a part that is not healthy or has an
order, a spare or a swap, with all of that device's parts and the
ids the part commands take.

mod_api.description: Generation and schema minor of this encoding.

quantum.description: The mod quantum index this snapshot was projected at.

MsgArgView.description:
One argument for a localized message.

The engine sends a stable message key plus these arguments, and the client
chooses the words.

A list of typed pairs stands in for a map, which the wire format lacks.

`is_number` picks the live slot. Numbers stay numbers on the wire because
Fluent needs a real number for plural selection and locale-aware number
formatting. A pre-formatted string would fix en-US grouping and break
plural rules in every language that inflects.

is_number.description: Selects which of `text` / `number` carries the value.

key.description: Placeholder name as it appears in the FTL source, without the `$`.

text.description:
Live when `is_number` is false. Already-resolved proper nouns
(customer names, site names) travel here, names are data, not
translation.

NetworkSegmentView.description:
A player-created network segment (VXLAN isolation overlay). Small
top-level list on `WorldSnapshot` (msgpack-only, like `host_pools`).
Customer membership is derived engine-side via `resolve_vrf`; the
client builds a host→segment view from `carrier_host_ids` /
`dedicated_host_ids`.

carrier_host_ids.description:
Distinct hosts carrying this segment's members' workloads, the
derived VTEP set, used for the "touches N hosts" blast-radius readout.

dedicated_free_disk_gb.description:
Free SSD (GB) summed over the dedicated host-set (`free_ssd_gb`). `0`
when logical-only.

dedicated_free_mem_mb.description:
Free memory (MB) summed over the dedicated host-set (`free_mb`). `0`
when logical-only.

dedicated_free_vcpu_milli.description:
Free physical vCPU (millivcpu) summed over the dedicated host-set,
`free_millivcpu` per host, the SAME accessor the per-host `HostView`
capacity reports, so a customer confined to this segment reads a meter
comparable to the fleet's. `0` when logical-only.

dedicated_free_vgpu_slices.description:
Free vGPU slices summed over the dedicated host-set (`free_vgpu_slices`
per host, the fleet capacity's accessor). `0` when logical-only.

dedicated_host_count.description:
Number of hosts dedicated to this segment. `0` = logical-only (the
customer lands anywhere in the fleet, so the prospect card reads the
fleet meter, not these figures). Same set as `dedicated_host_ids.len()`.

dedicated_host_ids.description: Hosts whose `admit` is this segment (physically dedicated).

dedicated_total_disk_gb.description: Total (eff) SSD (GB) of the dedicated host-set. `0` when logical-only.

dedicated_total_mem_mb.description: Total (eff) memory (MB) of the dedicated host-set. `0` when logical-only.

dedicated_total_vcpu_milli.description:
Total (eff/wear-adjusted nominal) vCPU (millivcpu) of the dedicated
host-set. `0` when logical-only.

dedicated_total_vgpu_slices.description:
Total vGPU slices of the dedicated host-set. `0` when logical-only or
when no dedicated host carries a GPU.

explicit_customer_ids.description: Customers explicitly pinned to this segment.

member_count.description:
Count of customers currently resolving to this segment (explicit
pins + tier-rule matches).

tier_rule.description:
SLA-tier auto-membership rule as a tier tag ("Bronze".."Platinum"),
or `None` when the segment only gathers explicit pins.

vni.description: VXLAN network identifier assigned at create time.

NetworkSettingsView.description:
Fabric-wide network policy toggles. Lives under `ServiceSettingsView`
for UI grouping but reads off `Engine` globals, not `ServiceSettings`.

auto_l3_enabled.description:
When `true`, every switch↔switch link between two ManagedL3
switches runs L3/Routed (ECMP, all-active, STP-exempt) instead of
bridged. Player can pin individual links to override. Mirrors
`Engine::auto_l3_enabled`; toggled via `SetAutoL3`.

PartsSnapshot.description:
The parts of ONE rack device (host, switch, gateway or security
appliance), pulled by `Request::InspectParts` when a console's Repair
tab opens and re-polled while it is open. Same shape for every kind.

components.description:
Every part, PSUs first, then disks, fans, DIMMs, CPUs, slot order
within a kind.

held_down.description:
The device is down and will stay down until a part is replaced
(as opposed to a power / outage window with a clock behind it).

held_reason.description:
Why `held_down` is true, as a stable tag the console maps to its own
i18n key -- never prose, so the wire carries no un-translatable
English (the same rule as `inv_status` and `inspection_state`).
`"psu_dark"` = no working corded PSU; `""` = generic hold (a dead
fan/CPU, or `held_down` false).

ports.description:
Per-port views, same shape as `HostView::ports` /
`SwitchView::ports` / `EddView::ports` so click resolvers,
inspectors, and cable renderers can treat patch panel ports as
first-class without a kind-specific branch.

A panel is PASSIVE, it negotiates nothing and lights no link LED, so
`state` stays `Down`, but **it is not IDLE**: a coupler is a cable's
direct peer, so the flow resolver mirrors the far end's throughput onto
it (`traffic/port_flow.rs`). The live rate rides `PortFlowView` on the
per-tick `DeviceFlowView` row, like every other ported device, and
`activity` here bands that same pair.

used_ports.description: How many of the panel's ports currently carry a cable.

sku_name.description:
SKU name from the catalog ("PSU 800W EPS", etc.). Empty when
the order was placed via `BuySpare { kind: ... }` fallback.

spec_label.description:
Pre-rendered spec label, "PSU 800W EPS", "Disk 4TB SAS 3.5\"",
"Fan 120mm 2000rpm". Buy-panel renders directly.

PlacementFailureView.description:
**The gate that bound a placement, with its numbers.** It answers "why is
my service short" with structured data.

`needed` and `available` are numbers in `unit`s of whatever the gate
measures: distinct hosts for a spread contract, MB for memory, GB for disk.
The client writes the wording. A capacity figure reported for a gate that
counts distinct hosts would send the player to buy RAM that fixes nothing.

The empty state is `code: ""`. It means the last placement attempt for this
service did not fail, so there is no gate to name.

available.description:
How many were actually available. For a capacity gate this is the MOST
any single surviving candidate had, so the difference reads as a real
gap rather than a fleet-wide total the unit cannot use anyway.

candidates.description:
How many hosts were still in the running when a CAPACITY gate bound,
the field that survived admission, homing, cordon, arch/accel and the
residency pins and actually reached the fit check.

**`considered - candidates` is the confinement signal.** "The roomiest
server has 2 GB" is true and useless when the tenant may only use 3 of
40 machines: the player looks at an idle 200 GB box and concludes the
game is broken, and "buy another host" is the wrong remedy anyway. The
two counts let the client pick between that sentence and "widen the
segment, or add a host to it", which is why both ship rather than one.

Only `placement_resource` defines it (`Binding::Resource.candidates`);
every other gate reports the count it narrowed to in `available`, so
this is 0 there.

code.description:
Stable `Binding::code()`, `placement_spread`, `placement_resource`,
`placement_no_hosts`, `placement_maintenance`, ... Empty when no gate
bound. The renderer branches on THIS, never on the prose.

considered.description: How many hosts entered the candidate scan, before any gate.

shortfall.description:
`Binding::shortfall()`, the one number a remedy is sized from ("buy 29
more servers"). 0 for categorical gates.

subject.description:
STABLE TOKEN naming the thing the gate is about, when it has one, the
resource (`Resource::tag`), the product a pool is not set to serve
(`ServiceClass::tag`), the required architecture / accelerator, the
pinned region / AZ id. Empty otherwise.

unit.description:
STABLE TOKEN for what `needed` / `available` are counted in: a
fault-domain slug (`FaultDomain::tag`, `host` / `switch` / `az` /
`region` / `power` / `router`) for a spread contract, a resource unit
(`Resource::unit_label`, `MB` / `GB` / `IOPS` / `slices`) for a
capacity gate, and `host` for the categorical gates, which all count
machines. The client turns this into a localized noun; it is
deliberately not one already.

PortAnchorView.description:
WHICH FAMILY of physical anchor on a device's baked model a cable endpoint
lands on. Paired with `anchor_ordinal` (the 0-based position WITHIN that
family) it is the endpoint's render identity, resolved ONCE by the
projection, which is the only side that knows the port layout.

**This exists because `port` is not an anchor name.** A device's `ports` is
ONE index space holding several physically unrelated bands: a host runs
built-in NICs, then PSU inlets, then module NICs; a switch runs data ports,
then inlets, then the MLAG keepalive jack, then stacking jacks; a patch
panel runs its front couplers then its rear terminations. `Port_<index + 1>`
is therefore only ACCIDENTALLY the right anchor, for the first band, and
silently wrong past it, engine index 6 on a 4-NIC/2-PSU host is not "the
7th NIC", it is "the first module NIC", which lives on the MODULE's own
cage anchor.

The offset between the two is NOT a constant to subtract: it is "how many
non-NIC ports precede this one", which differs per SKU (one PSU or two,
modules fitted or not). So it is resolved server-side against the device's
own SKU and named here, rather than re-derived by the renderer.

**Rides the ENDPOINT, not `PortView`.** `ports` is scopable detail
(`ViewportFilter::DetailBounded`) and is withheld from any device outside
the player's detail radius, while a cable is visible if EITHER end is,
so identity carried on a port would vanish for exactly the far-end device
whose anchor still has to resolve.

PortThroughput.description:
One port's throughput and lifetime counters.

Joins to the nested `ports[]` rows on `/api/v1/hosts`,
`/api/v1/network/switches`, `/api/v1/network/gateways` and
`/api/v1/network/appliances` by `port_id`, which `PortView` carries and which
is stable across snapshots. `owner_kind` + `owner_id` + `index` are the same
join spelled the other way round, for a consumer walking devices.

bytes_egress_total.description:
Lifetime bytes out. Non-decreasing within a session and PERSISTED, so a
loaded save carries its history rather than restarting from zero.

bytes_ingress_total.description: Lifetime bytes in. Same rules as `bytes_egress_total`.

gbps_rx.description:
Received throughput, Gbps, clamped to `link_capacity_gbps`. Full duplex,
so the ceiling is per direction and a saturated port legitimately reads
`gbps_tx + gbps_rx == 2 x link_capacity_gbps`.

index.description: Port index on that device, the same value as `PortView.index`.

link_capacity_gbps.description:
The rate this port's throughput was CLAMPED to, in Gbps: what the cage
can actually pass, which for a breakout trunk is the pool rather than one
leg. `0` for a passive port (patch-panel jack, IEC inlet), which is also
the case where no clamp was applied.

This is `Engine::port_rate_ceiling_gbps`, so it may differ from the
nested `PortView.link_capacity_gbps` on a trunk. Compare a rate against
THIS one.

link_flaps.description:
Times this port went Up to Down with a cable still seated, meaning the
link dropped and the player did not unplug it. A cable fault does not
count here: it sets `Errored`, which is sticky and never makes the
Up-to-Down transition. A high count points at the device at one end, not
at a marginal cable.

owner_id.description: Id of the owning device, within `owner_kind`.

owner_kind.description:
Device kind that owns this port: `"host"`, `"switch"`, `"gateway"`,
`"appliance"`, `"edd"` or `"patch_panel"`.

port_id.description: Stable engine port id, the same value as `PortView.port_id`.

PortView.description:
Per-physical-port readout. `peer` is the *other end* of the cable on this
port, None when the port is dark. The renderer uses `peer` to draw the
port label tooltip ("→ Switch S2 port 17") without needing the cable list.

active.description:
LINK TRUTH: a cable is seated AND this device is operational AND the
far-end device is operational (`build_world_ports_for_owner`:
`p.is_occupied() && entity_up && peer_live`).

**IT IS NOT A TRAFFIC FLAG, AND THREE PLACES SAID IT WAS.** The 59-batch
brief, and the `Uncovered` notes on this leaf in `fp_coverage.rs`, both
described it as "port-level traffic flag; derived from gbps" and
scheduled it for removal beside `gbps_tx` / `gbps_rx` on that basis. It
has never touched a throughput figure. `PortLed.activity` computes its
OWN `active` client-side from `state` plus flow and never reads this
field, which is what made the mix-up survivable and invisible.

**So it was KEPT when the two rates were removed.** It has a live reader
(`equipment_tooltip.gd`, the port link line), it costs one bit in capnp,
and `link` and `state` are both DERIVED FROM IT in the projection, a
port whose `port.state` is `Up` is published `Down` when this is false.
Removing it would have silently changed a link readout while claiming to
delete a duplicate of a throughput field.

Classified `Immediate` for the same reason `state` is: every input
(occupancy, own power, peer power) is in the port signature or behind a
discrete site.

activity.description:
Coarse activity band: 0 idle, 1 light, 2 busy. A port LED needs only the
band, and the client animates the flash. Plugging or unplugging a cable
ships the full view, so the band changes on the tick it happens. Exact
tx/rx rates would be unreadable at LED precision and cost bytes on every
port.

The per-tick rate is on `PortFlowView`, merged by port index. An open
console and the port tooltip read it there.

The engine owns the band thresholds, with hysteresis on the busy edge so
a rate parked on the boundary does not flip the band every tick.

The band is not part of `Port::structure_hash`, so a traffic change does
not count as a structural change.

breakout_used_gbps.description:
Breakout trunk pool, when this QSFP cage has been subdivided into
lower-speed legs (see `sim_core::breakout`). `breakout_capacity_gbps`
is > 0 ONLY while this port is an ACTIVE breakout trunk (it's the
pool size, e.g. 100 for a QSFP28 handing out 4×25 G); `used_gbps` is
the Gbps already committed to legs and `leg_count` how many legs are
seated. All three are 0 for an ordinary port, including a plain
QSFP cage with no legs yet.

This is the ONLY signal that lets the client tell a partially-used
breakout trunk apart from an empty port: both leave `cable_id ==
None` (the trunk's occupancy lives in the pool, not a single cable),
so without this a trunk with 1 of 4 lanes used reads as "empty" and
the player gets no cue that it can still take more legs.

cable_able.description:
Whether the *player* may cable this port. False for carrier-facing
ports (the edd WAN side, it's the auto-wired ISP handoff,
managed on the Internet panel, never patched). The diegetic
overlay refuses to start/finish a cable on a port where this is
false. Defaults true (snapshots are transient, never persisted).

cable_ids.description:
The cable ids attached to this port, occupancy is `!is_empty()`, which
drives the seated plug/module in the renderer (NOT `state`, which only
tints the LED). A normal port has 0 or 1; a breakout trunk has one per
leg, so it seats its QSFP module for the same reason any port seats its
plug. The first id is the primary (peer/jacket-colour). Stable across
deltas AND keyframes, so the trunk does not flicker.

color.description:
Jacket-colour id ("Orange" / "Blue" / …) of the cable plugged into
this port, resolved from that cable's `resolved_color()`, exactly
as `connector` is resolved from its kind. `""` when the port is
unwired. Lets the renderer tint the RJ45 plug boot to match the run.

connector.description:
`ConnectorKind::name()` for the connector seated at this port,
derived from the plugged cable's kind × the port's cage generation
(`ConnectorKind::resolve`). `"None"` when empty. Drives the renderer's
exact plug/transceiver GLB + seating so it can never seat (e.g.) an LC
duplex on a QSFP MPO port.

link_capacity_gbps.description:
Port-link capacity in Gbps (e.g. 1, 10, 25, 100). Pulled from
`Port.link_capacity_gbps`, the negotiated speed; equals the SKU rating
today and may shift later if cable kind reduces it.

media.description:
Physical media at the port face, from `Port.media`. One of
`"Rj45"` / `"SfpPlus"` / `"Sfp28"` / `"Qsfp28"` / `"QsfpDD"` /
`"Carrier"` / `"IecPower"` / `"PatchKeystone"`. Drives the
renderer's per-port plug geometry + boot offset.

port_id.description:
Stable engine port id. Lets the renderer cross-reference a port
across snapshots without rebuilding from (entity_id, index)
tuples. Zero when projection couldn't resolve to a Port (defensive).

state.description:
Operational state, from `Port.state`, one of "Down", "Up",
"Errored", "Disabled". Drives LED colour at the renderer.

ProspectSegmentFitView.description:
One prospect's serve verdict for ONE existing segment: the same rule as the
prospect's own `fit_*`, measured against the serviceable hosts that admit
each of its service classes under that segment's VRF and the prospect's
tier (dedicated hosts, plus open hosts the segment's pools do not claim).
Present for every segment, with or without dedicated hosts. The card reads
it instead of the shared `fit_*` when the player picks that segment.

fit_can_serve_now.description:
Every asked class fits the hosts admitting it, and the whole ask fits
their union, right now.

fit_over_capacity.description: A VM-load prospect that does not fit even oversubscribed.

fit_oversubscribed.description: Demand above physical vCPU but within the hosts' overcommit dial.

fit_recommendation.description:
Engine-classified one-liner for the segment, the twin of
`ProspectView.fit_recommendation`.

fit_vcpu_after_pct.description: vCPU / RAM fullness of those hosts after the prospect lands.

landing_free_vcpu_milli.description:
Free and total vCPU (millivcpu), RAM (MB), disk (GB) and vGPU slices of
the serviceable hosts admitting any of the prospect's classes under this
segment: the sum the verdict above reads, drawn as the card's meters.

segment_id.description: `NetworkSegmentView.id` of the segment this verdict is for.

ProspectServiceView.description:
Per-service detail for ONE service in a prospect's bundle, the
prospect-acceptance card's "what they actually want" line, for every
service kind (vm/fn/obj/db/lb/cdn/k8s), not just VMs. Mirrors the shape
of the service's demand contract; `vcpu`/`memory_mb`/`storage_gb` are 0
and `throughput_label`/`durability` are empty when the concept doesn't
apply to that kind (SCHEMA empty-state policy, 0/empty, not `Option`).

durability.description:
Replication / durability tier name ("Standard"/"High"/"Mission"/
"replicated"). Empty when the kind carries no durability contract.

gpu_mem_mb.description:
Per-unit GPU frame-buffer ask in MB (`VmSpec.vgpu.gpu_mem_mb`). 0 when
no GPU. Pairs with `vgpu_slices` on the demand line.

label.description: Plain-voice label (`ServiceClass::label`, falls back to the kind code).

requested_count.description:
Requested unit count, VM `target_count` / k8s `node_count` / 1 for
singleton services (Functions, Object Store, CDN, LB, managed DB).

storage_gb.description:
Storage magnitude (GB), object-store initial bucket / managed-DB
block + backup. 0 when the kind carries no storage ask.

throughput_label.description:
Service-specific rate, human & concise ("50 req/s",
"120 req/s · 8 KB/req"). Empty when the kind has no request rate.

vcpu.description: Per-unit vCPU. 0 when the kind has no compute shape of its own.

vgpu_slices.description:
Per-unit vGPU partition ask (`VmSpec.vgpu.slices`). 0 when the service
needs no GPU, the common case. Non-zero only for GPU personas (AI Lab /
VFX / genomics), whose VMs must land on a GPU host. Lets the card spell
out the GPU requirement on the demand line instead of hiding it.

block_gb_per_vm.description:
Per-VM block-volume size (GB). 0 when the ask carries no volume
(legacy templates / non-VM workloads). Billed via `BlockPricing`
alongside the VM's compute charge.

covering_segment_id.description:
Id of the segment whose `tier_rule` already claims this prospect's
tier, i.e. the segment the prospect would auto-join on signup via
tier-rule precedence. `0` = none (no tier-rule segment covers this
tier; the prospect would land on the Default shared segment). Lets
the prospect card offer "isolate into <existing segment>" without a
second round-trip. Mirrors the accept-path covering check.

covering_segment_name.description:
Display name of the covering segment (empty when `covering_segment_id`
is 0). Paired with the id so the card can label the existing-segment
option without a client-side lookup.

demands_air_gap.description: True when the prospect's archetype demands an air-gapped facility.

demands_audit_logs.description:
True when the prospect's archetype demands audit logging (a live
SIEM + audit feed). Surfaced as a requirement chip so a PCI /
government-contract prospect's otherwise-inexplicable rejection is
legible ("Requires: audit logging").

estimated_monthly_revenue_dollars.description:
List-price monthly run-rate this prospect would bill at signup,
projected from its VM workload (count × per-VM hourly × hours/month).
0 for non-VM-shaped prospects. Lets the customers lens show a
prospect's potential Revenue/hr before you sign them.

fault_ask_grain.description:
**The LEVEL behind that bool**, the kind of failure this prospect wants
to survive, as `FaultDomain::tag()`, and the most of themselves they
will accept losing to one, as a percentage.

Empty tag = the persona states no level and the bare bool above is the
whole ask, exactly as before.

On the PROSPECT card on purpose. "Copies kept apart" told a player
nothing they could act on and nothing they could check their site
against; "no more than half in one zone" is a promise they can decide to
take or decline BEFORE signing, which is the whole point of the card.
The engine owns the tag and the number, the client owns the wording.

fault_ask_max_share_pct.description: The share, 1..=100. Meaningless when `fault_ask_grain` is empty.

fit_can_serve_now.description:
True when the current fleet has free vCPU, memory **and** disk headroom
for this prospect's initial demand right now (no new hardware needed).

fit_over_capacity.description:
True only for a genuine over-capacity fit: a VM-load prospect that won't
fit even under overcommit (the "Over capacity, add hardware first"
verdict). Boolean twin of that string so the card's Accept-anyway confirm
gate keys off a field, not exact prose. False for no-VM / oversubscribed.

fit_oversubscribed.description:
True when accepting would push the fleet PAST physical into overcommit:
the initial VMs still fit under the host overcommit ceiling, but CPU is
shared and tenants may slow under load. Never a false "can't fit".

fit_recommendation.description:
Engine-classified one-liner for the card: "Comfortable" / "Tight fit" /
"Will run oversubscribed (CPU shared under load)" / "Over capacity, add
hardware first" / "Needs GPU hardware, add a GPU host first" /
"No VM load".

fit_ssd_after_pct.description:
The DISK axis, on the same basis as the two above. `contract_footprint`
computes `Resource::SsdGb` (an object-storage bucket, a CDN origin, a
DB's backup copies, a VM's block volume); without this axis a card asking
for 821 GB would show no disk meter at all and read "Comfortable" beside
it. 0.0 when the bundle asks for no bytes.

fit_vcpu_after_pct.description:
Capacity-fit verdict: projected
fleet VM utilization *after* accepting this prospect's initial demand,
on each axis. `1.0` = exactly full; `> 1.0` = would overcommit. Lets
the prospect card answer "can I actually serve this?" before signing.
0.0 for prospects with no VM workload.

gpu_slices_demand.description:
Total vGPU slices this prospect's initial VMs would reserve
(`initial_vm_count × per-VM slices`). 0 for non-GPU prospects. The
fleet-fit input the serve verdict weighs against free vGPU slices.

growth_ceiling_vms.description:
Growth ceiling (max VMs the customer can compound to) read from
the archetype's `growth.plateau_at_allocation`. 0 = no archetype
match or uncapped (Anchor / Enterprise). Renderer shows "may
grow to ~N" when > initial_vm_count.

initial_vm_count.description:
Initial VM count this prospect will request at signup. 0 when
the prospect doesn't run a VM workload (Functions / ObjectStore /
etc.), the renderer surfaces those via `services_summary`.

landing_free_vcpu_milli.description:
Free and total vCPU (millivcpu), RAM (MB), disk (GB) and vGPU slices of
the serviceable hosts THIS prospect can land on: open hosts plus pool
hosts whose admit filter accepts its workloads. The same host sum the
`fit_*` verdict reads, so the card's meters and its verdict cannot
disagree. Equals `CapacityView` on a fleet with no dedicated host.

memory_mb_per_vm.description: Per-VM memory (MB). 0 when no VM workload.

required_arch.description:
Raw CPU-arch requirement tag ("x86_64" / "arm64" / …) this prospect's
VM or K8s workload demands, or "" if arch-agnostic. A hard placement
gate: the card voices it (jargon "x86-64 hosts" vs plain "Intel/AMD
hosts") beside the compliance/air-gap chips. Godot maps the tag via
the `arch_req_<tag>` glossary key.

requires_fault_isolation.description:
True when the prospect's contract asks for fault isolation, copies kept
off a shared fault domain (redundancy tier > 1 host replica, or an
archetype requiring anti-affinity). Mirrors
`CustomerView.requires_fault_isolation` so the prospect "Must clear" card
and the accepted-customer Requirements row read the SAME key and cannot
drift. msgpack-only (ProspectView is not carried in capnp).

requires_gpu.description:
True when any of this prospect's VM services demands a GPU (vGPU
partition / `required_accelerator == Gpu`). Drives the card's GPU meter
and makes the serve verdict GPU-aware, a GPU tenant on a GPU-less fleet
reads "Needs GPU hardware", not a false "Comfortable".

requires_private_segment.description:
True when the prospect wants a private/isolated network segment
(VXLAN isolation) dedicated to its SLA tier. SOFT / recommended,
unlike audit-logging / air-gap it does NOT hard-reject signing; it's
satisfied by a private segment whose `tier_rule` matches this
prospect's `tier`. Surfaced as a "Recommended" chip, distinct in tone
from the hard requirement chips.

segment_fits.description:
The serve verdict against each existing segment, one entry per segment
(few), computed by the same rule as the `fit_*` above under that
segment's VRF. A card that picks a segment reads its entry here instead
of the shared `fit_*` above.

service_kinds.description:
Short-code service mix mirroring `CustomerView.service_kinds`
(subset of {"fn", "vm", "obj", "lb", "db", "cdn", "k8s"}). The ops-console
customer/prospect table renders these as upper-case chips, so a
prospect row reads the same as an active-customer row.

services.description:
Per-service detail for the WHOLE bundle, one entry per service the
prospect would sign for. The card renders each as a magnitude line so
non-VM prospects (object-store / DB / functions / ...) read as more
than a bare chip. Additive to the VM fields above, which still drive
the capacity-fit bar.

threat_exposure_weight.description:
What signing this prospect does to the facility's background threat,
`archetype.threat.exposure_weight`. See
`CustomerView::threat_exposure_weight` for the full rationale.

**On the PROSPECT it is the decision input, which is the whole point.**
Post-signing it is an explanation; here it is a choice. Ambient recon
scales with the roster, and the counterplay at a tier with no
purchasable mitigation is simply not signing the loud ones, which needs
the player to be told which those are.

threat_targeted.description:
True when this archetype can draw a TARGETED attack once signed,
`threat.attack_event_chance_per_month > 0`. See
`CustomerView::threat_targeted`.

vcpu_per_vm.description: Per-VM vCPU count. 0 when no VM workload.

RackFace.description:
Top vs bottom face of a rack, where a cable enters or exits the rack.
The top face leads to overhead trays and the bottom face to the underfloor
duct.

RackSide.description:
Vertical-strip side of a rack. Used for both cable-manager strips
(left or right of the U column) and the matching corner of a rack-edge
anchor. Distinct from `RoutingSide`, which is a single choice per
endpoint. A route can reference this side several times.

binding_key.description:
Symbolic key tying this rack to an authored scene node of the same
name. When set, `world_equipment_sync` binds `node.name ==
binding_key` and stamps the node's `entity_id`.
`None` for player-bought / procedurally-spawned racks.

depth_m.description:
Internal depth in metres. Drives the chassis-fit check at
switch placement (`SwitchSku::chassis_depth_m()`) and lets the
rack inspector show "this is a 450 mm wall-mount cabinet, the
700 mm spine you ordered won't fit." Resolved engine-side via
`Rack::depth_m()`, which supplies the standard-DC fallback.

fabric_az_id.description:
The zone this rack's hosts are WIRED into: the zone of the nearest
router their switch chain reaches, else `az_id`. Players
cable a colo's two zones together, which is legal; when this differs
from `az_id` the rack shares the other zone's fault domain and the
client says so. Equal to `az_id` on a single-zone site and until the
first sample after a load.

floor_slot.description:
Index into the AZ's rack-slot grid where this rack physically
stands. Renderer looks up `RackSlot{N}` Marker3D anchors under
the world scene to place it. `None` for tiers that use authored
aisle layouts instead of the slot grid.

held.description:
Is anybody carrying it? Separate from `held_by` because
`PlayerId::LOCAL` is `0` (see `DeliveryView::held`).

held_by.description:
MULTIPLAYER: which player is carrying this crate. Meaningless unless
`held` is true. Only meaningful while `pending_placement` is true.

The renderer skips a held crate's shipping-zone prop and excludes it
from the pile layout, so both clients agree about which crates are on
the floor and where (the pile is indexed by position in the remaining
list).

Session state: `load_reported` clears it, so this is always `0` on the
first snapshot after a load.

pending_placement.description:
True while this rack is a bought-but-not-installed crate in the
shipping zone. The renderer draws a crate prop (not a rack
chassis) and the player carries it to a floor slot via
`InstallRack`.

resale_dollars.description:
Resale value if the rack is uninstalled and sold at the sell
zone. Surfaced so the carry HUD can show "Sell for $X".

used_u.description:
U slots actually consumed in this rack, counting EVERY rack occupant:
hosts, switches, patch panels, security appliances, EDDs and gateways.
Same population as `Engine::occupied_u`, sourced from the one-pass
`Engine::occupied_u_by_rack`.

Do not re-derive this client-side by summing `u_size` over the `hosts`
array: that misses everything racked that is not a server, and a second
copy of the occupant list drifts.

wall_mount.description:
True for the wall-mounted cabinet that ships as a fixture of the
Garage / SmallColo rooms. Renderer binds the authored `WallRack`
node to this rack's id (no procedural visual) and the inspector
surfaces AZ-level edd + floor-tower context above / below the
U stack.

RailDepth.description:
Front-vs-rear position of a side-panel RAIL hole (`SidePanelHole_
<side>_<depth>_<height>` in the authored rack mesh). Structurally
identical to `RoofHoleSide` but kept as its own type: the rail-hole
family and the roof-hole family must never cross-pair (a rear rail
hole is never the same anchor as a rear roof cutout), and reusing
`RoofHoleSide` here would make that accidental aliasing possible.

RailHeight.description:
Top-vs-bottom position of a side-panel rail hole. `Top` holes thread
a cable rack-to-rack along a row (`RouteAnchor::RailHole` /
`RackAnchor::RailHole`). `Bottom` holes instead drop into the
underfloor duct (a plain `RouteAnchor::Point`). The two heights are never
interchangeable.

backbone_capacity_gbps.description:
Capacity of ONE lane of ONE trunk (Gbps): every pair, each direction.
Not the site total; compare it with a lane in `az_trunks`.

backbone_saturated.description: True when ANY lane of ANY trunk on the site is saturated.

RelocationGateView.description:
One unlock gate for relocating to the next site, with live progress,
drives the relocation-screen checklist. `current`/`target` are pre-
formatted for display (e.g. "3, 200" vs "5, 000", "0.42" vs "0.40").

RelocationOfferView.description:
The offer to relocate to the next site (the funded-relocation model).
`available` is false when the scenario has no next progression step
(final tier / no ladder), the client hides the relocate affordance.
`ready` = every gate met. The money math (`funding_grant` + estimated
`liquidation` = `new_capital`) and the per-tenant `tenants` list power the
switch screen; the client does the per-window churn preview client-side.

projected_new_capital_dollars.description:
`cash + funding_grant + estimated_liquidation`, the starting capital
on the new floor, shown on the switch screen.

RelocationTenantView.description:
One tenant's exposure to a relocation's migration window. The client
renders the live "won't wait" list + MRR-at-risk by filtering these to
`patience_hours < selected_window_hours`. Sorted least-patient first.

monthly_dollars.description: Approx monthly recurring revenue at risk if this tenant leaves.

patience_hours.description: This tenant churns on commit if the chosen window exceeds this.

RelocationWindowView.description:
One migration-window choice on the relocation screen. `key` is the
`MigrationWindow` variant name sent back as `UpgradeFacility { window }`.

ReservationView.description:
A host RESERVATION, a distinct `Admit` filter (scope × service) currently in
use, plus the host ids carrying it. Drives the fleet-by-job / homing
"Machines" axis: which machines are reserved for which scope×service. Open
hosts (`admit == None`) are NOT reservations and never appear here.

Enum-ish fields are encoded as strings (StrField), so this introduces NO new
wire enum. `scope_kind` is one of "any" | "default" | "vrf" | "tier";
`scope_id` is the VRF id when `scope_kind == "vrf"` (else 0); `scope_tier`
is the SLA tier tag when `scope_kind == "tier"` (else ""); `service` is
"any" or the `ServiceClass` tag ("vm"/"db"/"obj"/"fn"/"k8s"/"cdn"/"lb").

`WorldSnapshot.reservations` carries these on the msgpack keyframe only
(like `subnets` / `segments`), no per-tick capnp cost.

host_count.description: Count of hosts carrying this filter (`host_ids.len()`).

host_ids.description: Host ids carrying this exact `Admit` filter. Sorted ascending.

RevenueBreakdownView.description:
Lifetime revenue ledger split by service kind, projected from
`Engine::revenue_breakdown`. Sum of fields equals
`topbar.total_revenue_dollars`. Drives the dashboard's Services
drilldown: each service's row reads its bucket here, tier-locked
services that haven't been sold yet render at $0.

platform_fee.description: Flat per-tier platform/support fee, itemised out of `vms_dollars`.

RoofHoleSide.description:
Front-rear axis selector for the rack roof and floor cutouts. A 2-post
rack typically has a front and a rear cable cutout in its roof. This enum
picks which one a `RackFace::Top` (or future `Bottom`) anchor uses.

`RackSide::{Left, Right}` covers the lateral axis only. Without this
field a cable through the rear hole would be drawn at the front hole.

RouteAnchor.description:
Player-side route anchor, the flat list form that the LayCableThreaded
command uses. It differs from `RackAnchor` in that strip and edge anchors
carry `rack_id`, so the engine can group consecutive same-rack anchors into
per-rack threads. Tray segments (and future ceiling-mount segments)
connect one rack's thread to the next.

oneOf.description:
The engine assigns this from `CableKind::lane()` at lay time. The
player never sets it, so it is `None` on every player-submitted
command and filled in once the engine groups this into a
`RackAnchor`.

Marker/channel role: see `StripAnchorRole`. `None` from the player
and on every anchor the engine stores; only a role-bearing anchor
from an older save carries a value.

slot.description:
Next free index in the `(side, u_band, lane)` pool, assigned by the
engine at lay time. The player never sets it.

oneOf.description:
Front vs Rear roof cutout for `face: Top` anchors. `None`
lets the renderer pick (Front by convention). Player commands
from a clipped roof-hole pin set this to the marker's
authored side.

Tray pass-through. `tray_id` is a `cable_tray::TrayId`. Used for the
inter-rack segments of a route: the cable leaves a rack via an
EdgeCorner, runs through one or more Tray anchors, then enters the next
rack via another EdgeCorner.

Tray.description:
Tray pass-through. `tray_id` is a `cable_tray::TrayId`. Used for the
inter-rack segments of a route: the cable leaves a rack via an
EdgeCorner, runs through one or more Tray anchors, then enters the next
rack via another EdgeCorner.

slot.description:
Bundle slot within the tray, assigned by the engine when it emits
the snapshot. Like the manager-strip `slot` it can change between
snapshots and is not stored on the cable. `None` from the player.

oneOf.description:
A raw world position the cable threads through, not tied to any
engine entity. It lets a tray run placed in the scene act as a cable
waypoint without the engine owning a tray entity. The engine stores
the point so the cable redraws through it. It is a geometric waypoint
only, with no neatness or heat accounting.

Point.description:
A raw world position the cable threads through, not tied to any
engine entity. It lets a tray run placed in the scene act as a cable
waypoint without the engine owning a tray entity. The engine stores
the point so the cable redraws through it. It is a geometric waypoint
only, with no neatness or heat accounting.

oneOf.description:
A side-panel rail hole. See `RackAnchor::RailHole`. This is the flat
player-command form, and it carries `rack_id` like `Strip` and `Edge`
so the engine can group it into the right per-rack thread.

RailHole.description:
A side-panel rail hole. See `RackAnchor::RailHole`. This is the flat
player-command form, and it carries `rack_id` like `Strip` and `Edge`
so the engine can group it into the right per-rack thread.

SaleRecordView.description:
One historical sale, oldest first. Renderer reads this for the
finance-tab "Sales" rollup and the "what did I get for it" tooltip.

ScrubOfferView.description:
One catalog row this site is offered, priced AT THIS SITE (the fixed fee
resolved against `FloodProtectionView.protected_gbps`, per
`sim_core::scrub::ScrubPlan::monthly_dollars`). Every plan scrubs without
limit; tiers differ in leak, latency and price.

latency_added_ms.description:
Milliseconds the scrubbing hop adds to every served internet request
(`ScrubPlan::latency_added_ms`).

leak_pct.description:
The plan's BASE/display leak, percent (`ScrubPlan::leak_frac * 100`),
what the buy card quotes. The live leak wanders inside
`[leak_min_pct, leak_max_pct]` tick to tick (D15); this is the
display figure.

monthly_dollars.description:
This plan's FIXED monthly fee AT THIS SITE: flat base + per protected
Gbps x `FloodProtectionView.protected_gbps`. Clean traffic is billed on
top at `per_clean_gb_microcents`.

per_clean_gb_microcents.description:
The tier's per-clean-GB rate in microcents/GB, the resolved figure
(`Engine::scrub_clean_gb_microcents`: the scenario override, else the
tier's own rate). 0 for Proxy, which has no per-GB charge.

ServiceDemandView.description:
Demand vs fulfilment for one (customer, service) pair. Requested shape
mirrors the service's demand contract (`VmDemand`/`ManagedDbDemand`/...);
`vcpu`/`memory_mb`/`accelerator`/`durability` are 0 or empty when the
concept doesn't apply to that service kind (for example `durability` is
empty for VMs and `vcpu` is 0 for CDN). `region_id` is 0 when the customer
has no data-residency requirement.

accelerator.description:
Required accelerator name (`Accelerator::name`), empty when none
required.

durability.description:
Durability/replication tier name (Object Store bucket, managed DB
backup bucket). Empty when the service carries no durability
contract.

gap.description:
`requested_count.saturating_sub(provisioned_count)`, the
at-a-glance shortfall the inspector reads instead of subtracting.

memory_mb.description: Per-unit RAM requested, MB. 0 when not applicable.

placement.description:
The gate that bound the last placement attempt for this service, with
numbers. `code` empty = nothing bound. See `PlacementFailureView`.

provisioned_count.description: Live-capacity unit count backing the service right now.

reason.description:
`ProbeReason::label()`, why `state` isn't `Healthy`/`Ok`. A
PRE-RENDERED English sentence with no magnitudes; kept for
compatibility, but `placement` is what a card should size a remedy
from.

PROSE. Display fallback only, branch on `reason_tag`.

reason_args.description: The facts `reason_key` is resolved with. Empty when `reason_key` is.

reason_key.description:
Message key for the reason sentence when it carries NUMBERS the static
`label-probe-<reason_tag>` line cannot (the spread advisory, key
`label-spread-note`); empty otherwise. With `reason_args` it is the
sentence the client resolves in the reader's language; `reason` above is
its pre-rendered English twin for consumers that resolve no keys.

reason_tag.description:
`ProbeReason::tag()`, the STABLE slug behind `reason` (`"Ok"`,
`"FleetCapacityExhausted"`, ...), same shape and intent as
`FindingView.kind_tag`. The client tests `reason_tag != "Ok"` for
"has a problem" and resolves the sentence from
`label-probe-<reason_tag>`.

This field exists so the client never compares against `reason`
itself (see the note on that field and `ProbeReason::label`): that
comparison is untranslatable AND breaks the day `Ok`'s wording moves.

replicas_held.description:
Redundant copies the fleet ACTUALLY holds. 0 when `replication_tag` is
empty.

This is a SEPARATE pair from `provisioned_count`/`requested_count` on
purpose. Those are the LIVENESS reading, and for object storage they are
binary by design (`Engine::data_plane_counts` carves the class out, with
the reasoning, so that a serving-but-under-replicated bucket cannot route
into `service_shortfall_reason` and raise a second incident telling the
player to add compute). Overloading them for this one class would give
one field two meanings depending on `class_tag`, the exact defect family
`reason_tag` exists to kill, and would silently change what every
existing consumer of the liveness pair reads.

Byte-identical to the numerator `Engine::object_store_replication`
computes and `note_object_store_replication` opens the typed
`ObjectStoreUnderReplicated` incident with, so the customer page and the
incident cannot quote different counts for one bucket.

replicas_target.description:
Redundant copies the CONTRACT calls for, the customer's durability tier
(`Engine::object_store_effective_rf`). 0 when `replication_tag` is empty.
`replicas_held < replicas_target` is under-replication.

replication_tag.description:
**What `replicas_held`/`replicas_target` COUNT**, or empty when this
service has no redundancy contract of its own. `"copies"` for object
storage, durable copies of the bucket's bytes.

THE key a client branches on. It must never test `class_tag == "obj"`
(which hard-codes today's one class into every consumer) nor read the
prose beside it: engine ships the fact + a stable tag, client writes the
sentence. Same split as `reason_tag` / `state_tag` above.

requested_count.description:
Requested unit count (VM target_count / k8s node_count / 1 for
singleton services like Object Store, CDN, LB, managed DB).

state.description:
`ProbeState::label()`, Healthy/Degraded/Down/Unservable.

PROSE. Display fallback only, branch on `state_tag`.

state_tag.description:
`ProbeState::tag()`, the STABLE slug behind `state` (`"Healthy"` /
`"Degraded"` / `"Down"` / `"Unservable"`). This is what a client
branches on; it resolves its own word through
`label-probe-state-<state_tag>`. Rewording or localizing `state` must
never change what renders.

vcpu.description:
Per-unit vCPU requested. 0 when the service kind has no compute
shape of its own (Object Store, CDN, LB).

ServiceGateView.description:
