A service-class investment gate: whether
the class is sellable and, if not, what it costs to light up via
`PlayerCommand::InvestInService`.

affordable.description:
Cash on hand covers `unlock_cost_dollars` (only meaningful while
`enabled` is false).

enabled.description: Currently sellable (default-enabled or already invested in).

label_eng.description:
Engineer-voice label, "Object storage (S3-style)" / … (jargon on).
Renderer picks `label` vs `label_eng` by jargon mode.

offering.description:
"" for the built-in kind's own row. A pack service offering's row
carries its id, `<mod_id>:<item>`, which `InvestInService` takes as
`service`; its `class_tag` is the kind it runs as and both labels are
its shop name.

unlock_cost_dollars.description: One-time cost to enable when locked. 0 when default-enabled.

ServiceMarginView.description:
One service's slice of a tenant's gross margin, `sim_engine::business::
cost_attribution::ServiceMargin` on the wire.

ServicePlaneView.description:
Per-service control-plane + data-plane status, for the ops-console Services
page. One per host-bound `ServiceClass` when the
service plane is enabled. The renderer picks `label` vs `label_eng` by
jargon mode.

agent_vcpu_milli.description:
Per-host data-plane agent cost (config, surfaced so the page can show
and, later, tune it).

control_plane_host_ids.description: Hosts running a control-plane member (one per HA replica).

healthy.description: Control plane reachable (≥1 member up + reachable).

need_vcpu_milli.description:
Fleet-scaled control-plane compute need (millivcpu, mem_mb), the "your
control plane has to grow with your fleet" number.

overloaded.description: Outgrew the host it runs on, needs a bigger host or more replicas.

replicas_configured.description: Configured HA replica count (1 = single instance / SPOF).

replicas_floor.description:
Scenario-imposed minimum replicas, the player can't tune below this
(≥1). Drives the replica spinner's lower bound.

serving_hosts.description: Hosts running a data-plane agent (= hosts serving this class).

shards.description:
Horizontal shard count, `1` = fits one host; `>1` = the control
plane outgrew a single host and split across N to relieve load.

ServiceRevenueRateView.description:
One service kind's share of the fleet's last-hour revenue, in
[`CustomersSummary::service_last_hour`].

Kind plus magnitude, never a tenant count: `CustomerView::service_kinds` is
on the row every session already holds AND is on neither rotated half, so the
roster can still count buyers at full freshness. Shipping that count here too
would make a disagreement between the two representable across two separately
omittable sections, which is the rule [`CustomerRankView`] states.

kind.description:
Short-code service kind: `ServiceConfig::kind_label`, matching
`CustomerView::service_kinds`'s vocabulary (`vm`, `obj`, `db`, `lb`,
`cdn`, `fn`, `k8s`).

`value_type = String` because `StrField` is `Cow<'static, str>` and
utoipa's `ToSchema` wants `Clone` on the inner type, which `str` is not.
The established annotation in this file; see `ScenarioView::difficulty`.

last_hour_dollars.description:
This kind's share of the fleet's last-hour revenue, dollars. See
[`CustomersSummary::service_last_hour`] for what "share" means (an even
split).

ServiceSettingsView.description:
Renderer-friendly mirror of `sim_core::service_settings::ServiceSettings`.
Strings instead of enums so the GDScript schema can consume them
without a separate enum class. One sub-view per service section.

network.description:
Fabric-wide network policy. Not per-service: these are
datacenter-level switches surfaced on the ops-console Network tab.

catalog.description: Catalog entries the player can order from.

pending_orders.description: Outstanding orders in transit, buy-panel renders ETAs.

baseline_lead_hours.description: Baseline lead time from the SKU.

effective_capex_dollars.description:
Effective capex after macro-event multipliers, what the
player actually pays right now.

effective_lead_hours.description:
Effective lead time after macro multipliers, what the player
will actually wait if they order now.

sku_name.description:
SKU display name, "PSU 800W EPS", etc. Identifier the
player picks via `BuySpare { sku_name }`.

traits.description: Personality trait names (e.g. "Gifted", "Flaky"). Empty for none.

StrandedVmView.description:
One stranded VM, its host lost reachability and the customer's
redundancy tier is `Single`, so no auto-failover applies. Migration
picker consumes these directly.

az_id.description:
AZ the source host lives in. Migration targets must share this
id (Single tier is AZ-pinned). Surfaced so the renderer can
scope the target list without re-joining tables.

host_id.description:
The host the VM is currently pinned to, unreachable but still
powered up. Renderer displays it as the "from" side of the
migration picker.

vcpu.description:
VM workload footprint, same fields the bin-packer checks
against a candidate host's free capacity. The picker renders
"needs 4 vCPU · 8 GB · 20 GB" so the player can read why a
half-empty host won't accept the VM.

vm_id.description:
VM identity (`VmId(u64)` flat). Passed back to the engine via
`PlayerCommand::MigrateVm { vm_id, target_host_id }`.

StripAnchorRole.description:
Structural role of one `StripBand`/`Strip` anchor: which part of a
manager-strip run it represents. `Marker` is a finger-gap entry or exit
and `Channel` is an interior manager-runway position.

**Kept for old saves only: nothing sets this.** On load the engine
collapses any role-bearing run back to the single role-less anchor. The
engine stores what the player clicked, and the renderer decides at draw
time how a cable threads a manager between two clicks.

The variants stay so a role-bearing anchor from an older save round-trips
through the wire codec unchanged. `None` is the value every live anchor
carries.

SubnetView.description:
An L2 broadcast domain (subnet), the finer isolation grain BELOW the VRF: a
VRF is the routed L3 boundary, a subnet is one L2 segment within it, keyed
one-per-`ServiceClass` (so a tenant running VMs + Functions + K8s + a managed
DB has four sibling subnets, each independently dedicatable). Small top-level
list on `WorldSnapshot` (msgpack keyframe-only, exactly like `segments` /
`host_pools`; subnets change rarely, so they never ride the per-tick capnp
delta). Empty until the network-isolation model mints any subnet.

carrier_host_ids.description:
Hosts physically CARRYING this subnet's members, the distinct host ids
running the resident UNITS homed to this subnet, every product included
(function containers too). The L2VNI
(service-subnet) analog of
`NetworkSegmentView.carrier_host_ids` (the VRF-grain equivalent); lets
the netview overlay colour hosts by which L2VNI they carry, not just
which VRF. Sorted ascending, deduped. Empty until members are homed.

dedicated_host_ids.description:
Hosts physically dedicated to this subnet, those whose `admit` filter is
exactly this subnet's `(vrf, class)` (`{scope: L3vni(vrf), service:
Service(class)}`). Empty when the subnet is logical-only.

l2vni.description:
L2 VXLAN Network Identifier for this subnet's broadcast domain (minted
from a range disjoint from the VRF L3 VNIs).

member_count.description:
Count of resident UNITS currently homed to this subnet, one per placed
unit whose `Engine::unit_subnet` is this one, whatever its product.

One grain for every product: a 5-node cluster reads 5, each database
copy counts once, and a Functions subnet counts its containers.

routes_via.description:
How this subnet's cross-subnet (east-west) traffic is ROUTED out of its
L2VNI, the first-hop router serving its carrier hosts (`Engine::
first_hop_router` on the lowest-id carrier). One of:
  * `"switch"`, a distributed anycast L3 leaf routes it LOCALLY (resilient:
    survives an edge-gateway death);
  * `"gateway"`, CENTRALIZED at the edge gateway (a pure-L2 fabric hairpins
    cross-subnet traffic up to it, so a non-HA gateway is the SPOF for the
    tenant's tier-to-tier traffic);
  * `""`, no live L3 router on the path (cross-subnet traffic is
    PARTITIONED), or a logical-only subnet with no carrier hosts yet.
Lets the segments/isolation lens show a tenant WHERE their tiers route and
flag the pure-L2 cross-subnet SPOF proactively, not just via the
`InterSubnetPartition` incident once it breaks.

service.description:
The resident service class this subnet carries, the isolation grain, as
a `ServiceClass` tag ("vm"/"fn"/"obj"/"db"/"cdn"/"k8s"/"lb").

vrf_id.description: The VRF this subnet routes within. `0` is the Default shared VRF.

SwitchPairView.description:
An MLAG pair, two switches peered to present one LACP partner.

Small top-level list, msgpack-only, exactly like `lags`: pair counts are
single-digit and the content only moves on a structural change, so it is
keyframe-only and costs nothing per tick. Per-switch membership rides
`SwitchView.pair_id` for the cheap "which pair is this box in" question.

members.description:
Exactly two, primary first. Not a `Vec` on the engine side either,
MLAG has precisely two peers.

protected.description:
False whenever the pair is not delivering the redundancy it was bought
for. Drives the SPOF chip, and is TRUE only for `Healthy`, a pair
running without a keepalive works, and is still a single point of
failure, which is the whole thing the indicator exists to say.

status.description:
`"Healthy"` / `"NoKeepalive"` / `"SecondarySuspended"` / `"SplitBrain"`
/ `"MemberDown"`. See `sim_engine::switch_pair_ops::SwitchPairStatus`
for what each means, in particular that losing the peer-link with a
keepalive up is the SAFE case, not a split.

SwitchTopoRole.description:
Topology-derived classification for a switch's position in the fabric.
Distinct from the catalog SKU's `sim_core::switch::SwitchRole`, which
describes the product class. This one comes from actual wiring at
snapshot time:

- `Edge`, switch with at least one host-NIC cable. The leaf layer.
- `Core`, no hosts, but cabled to a gateway / patch panel. The
  border-handoff switch.
- `Spine`, no hosts, no gateway; cabled only switch-to-switch.
  Intra-fabric backbone.
- `Agg`, fallback / intermediate (no hosts, no gateway, no peers).

Serialised as snake_case so the GDScript renderer reads
`"edge"`/`"core"`/`"spine"`/`"agg"` directly.

broadcast_storm.description:
`true` when this switch is caught in a broadcast storm: a loop
through an unmanaged switch with no STP to break it. The switch
forwards nothing until a cable is pulled. Drives a critical console
state, distinct from saturation. (Switch CLASS is not duplicated
here; resolve it via `sku_name` to `SwitchSkuView.switch_class`.)

egress_gbps.description:
Smoothed directional egress in Gbps, **NORTHBOUND ONLY**: what this
switch sends toward its uplinks. Pairs with `ingress_gbps`.

**This is not "what the switch transmitted" and must not be shown as
if it were; use `total_egress_gbps` for that.** Two deliberate facts make them
differ. It is OFFERED load and uncapped, where a port counter is
clamped to what the wire negotiated (`sim_core::port::clamp_to_ceiling`),
so a saturated switch reads higher here than its ports can sum to. And
east-west is kept out of it by the plane decision in
`traffic::east_west`, because `Switch::saturated`, the edge `dio`
aggregation and the uplink waterfall all read it as a northbound trunk
meter; a leaf whose server-to-server chatter never heads north would
otherwise report trunk saturation and inflate the WAN line.

fabric_capacity_gbps.description:
Switching fabric (backplane) capacity. The aggregate cross-port
throughput ceiling, independent of trunk uplink. Cheap T1
switches oversubscribe heavily; datacenter SKUs are full
non-blocking.

fabric_load_gbps.description:
Smoothed full-duplex fabric load: `egress + ingress + east-west`, each
independently smoothed. Compared against `fabric_capacity_gbps`:
when this exceeds capacity the fabric ASIC drops packets. The
saturation metric, not the directional metric.

The east-west term is why this can exceed `egress + ingress`.

fabric_saturated.description:
`true` when fabric load exceeds `fabric_capacity_gbps`. Drives drops
independent of trunk saturation.

fabric_utilisation.description:
`fabric_load_gbps / fabric_capacity_gbps`. Folded ONCE in the projection (`build_switch_view_at`) so
every fabric-meter panel reads the same fraction instead of each
re-deriving `load / cap` locally (`godot/tests/test_source_lints.gd`'s
`test_client_side_traffic_ratios_do_not_grow` guard). `[0, 1+]`, NOT
clamped: a value above 1 is the reader's own signal that the fabric is
over its rated ceiling, same range `saturated` already implies. 0 when
`fabric_capacity_gbps` is 0 (never divides by zero). A switch has no
DPI derate, so this is `capacity_of(SwitchFabric)`, the same ceiling
as `fabric_capacity_gbps` above; see
`sim_engine::transit::saturation::effective_ceiling_gbps`.

ingress_gbps.description:
Smoothed directional ingress in Gbps: bytes arriving from
upstream/peers. Mirrors `egress_gbps`, with the same two caveats.

keepalive_port_index.description:
`PortView::index` of this switch's MLAG keepalive jack, when it has one.

ON THE VIEW BECAUSE THE ONLY OTHER SOURCE IS THE PORT ARRAY, WHICH IS
SCOPABLE. `cable_renderer._refresh_keepalive_index` learns the jack
by walking EVERY switch's ports fleet-wide looking for `label == "PAIR"`
("this renderer stores no snapshot"), and `multimesh_hardware._write_conn`
reads the same label to seat the connector. The keepalive is minted ABOVE
the data + power ports, so its numeric index moves with a model's PSU
count and no `Port_<N>` anchor can track it, a missing entry does not
degrade, it lands the peer-link cable on the wrong hole. Structural: it
moves only when a switch is bought, sold or re-SKU'd.

`None` = no keepalive jack. 0 is a REAL index, so this cannot be a
sentinel int.

link_count.description: Cabled data ports, ALWAYS present. See `HostView::link_count`.

model_sku.description:
The base SKU whose model renders this one. Empty means `sku_name`.
See `HostView::model_sku`.

monthly_opex_dollars.description:
Live projected monthly opex ($/mo), running fee + chassis power +
this switch's seated-optic draw. Mirrors the host console's
`monthly_opex_dollars` read.

on_shelf.description:
True when this is a Desktop-class switch sitting on a 1U cantilever
shelf inside a rack. The renderer spawns a `shelf_1u_cantilever.glb`
in the same U slot and centers the switch on the tray; engine-side
the implicit shelf occupies the slot via `effective_u_size()`.
Mutually exclusive with `on_wall` (a switch can't be both).

on_wall.description: True for wall-shelf switches (garage tier, no rack required).

pair_id.description:
MLAG pair this switch belongs to; 0 when unpaired.

Per-switch on purpose, and NOT a duplicate of anything the edge view
owns: `TopoEdgeView` can say "these two links are one bond", it cannot
say "this switch is a member of pair N".

Structural, so it rides `struct_fp` and never the telemetry half.

pair_role.description:
`"Primary"` / `"Secondary"` within the pair, `""` when unpaired.

Which member forwards alone when the peer-link drops, so the console
can say WHY one switch is quiet. Derived from member ordering (lowest
id primary, the engine's stable analogue of the lower LACP
system-id), never stored, so it cannot drift from the suspension rule.

port_capacity_gbps.description: Per-port line speed (Gbps). Used by the renderer to color-code port LEDs.

ports.description:
Per-physical-port readouts. One entry per `port_count`, sourced
from `engine.ports` filtered by owner. Populated for the
workbench inspector (T1 has no rack but still wants per-port
LEDs / speed badges / activity blink). Rack-resident switches
are also surfaced here for renderers that don't open a full
`RackInspectSnapshot`.

SCOPABLE DETAIL: `None` = withheld from this session,
`Some([])` = genuinely portless. Full rules on `HostView::ports`.
Ports dominate a `SwitchView`'s size, which is why they are scoped.

power_feeds.description:
Connected AC cord count. >= 2 = PSU-failure resilience at
`redundant_psu_overhead_w` extra draw per extra cord.

powered.description:
At least one AC cord seated (or none required). False = dark
until the player plugs it in. Mirrors the engine's `powered`.

psu_dark.description:
True when no corded PSU can deliver power (every PSU Failed, or every
CORDED inlet's PSU Failed): every lamp reads dark, `indicator` forced
`Off` alongside it. See `HostVisual.psu_dark`
for the full rule; single source of truth: `sim_project`'s switch
projection.

rack_id.description: Rack id when rack-mounted; 0 for wall-shelf switches.

role.description:
Topology-derived role: where this switch sits in the fabric.
Computed each snapshot from cable wiring (NOT the SKU's static
`sim_core::switch::SwitchRole`, which describes the catalog
class: `Desktop`/`Access`/`ToR`/`Leaf`/`Aggregation`/`Spine`).
NetView uses this to pick "edge switch" / "core switch" sub-labels.

start_u.description: Starting U slot when rack-mounted; 0 when on a wall shelf.

total_egress_gbps.description:
**Everything the switch sent, server-to-server included.**

The sum of the switch's own ports' TX, both planes: exactly what its
port table adds up to. It is the figure a console charts, because
`egress_gbps` alone cannot move for traffic that never heads north: a
leaf pushing server-to-server showed every port row alive under a flat
line.

It is NOT `egress_gbps + east_west/2` (the backplane row credits a
switched byte once, not in and out). `snapshot::switch_port_totals` is
the guard that pins it to the port rows.

total_ingress_gbps.description:
Everything the switch received, server-to-server included.
Mirrors `total_egress_gbps`.

ThreatClassView.description:
Per-class resolution: how much came in, how much the fleet mitigated, what
leaked. `class` is the slug ("volumetric"/"protocol"/"application"/
"intrusion").

ALL FOUR classes are carried, Application included. L7 has no on-prem
defender, but its residual drives real tenant impact, so hiding the row
would leave the player with damage and no readout. It ships with
`edge_defensible: false`: visible pressure, with the explicit "no edge
defender exists" state that explains why no purchase on the shop shelf
changes the number.

edge_defensible.description:
Can ANY on-prem edge box defend this class (`AttackClass::defended_by`
is non-empty)? True for Volumetric / Protocol / Intrusion, a scrubber,
firewall or IPS exists to buy. False for Application: L7 is the
customer-purchased WAF service, and by design nothing at our edge
touches it, so `mitigated` is structurally 0 and `residual` is the full
incoming pressure. The renderer must say so plainly rather than let the
row read as an unbought upgrade.

label.description:
Two-voice display labels (plain | engineer), picked by jargon mode,
same pattern as `ServiceGateView`. The renderer does not hardcode
"Volumetric"/"Flood"/etc.; it reads these.

mitigated_at_gateway.description:
Attribution of `mitigated` by defender type, how much was blocked at a
gateway's built-in firewall vs at a dedicated security appliance. Lets
the ops-lens show "blocked at gateway X / at appliances Y / leaked Z"
without per-box drill-down. Sums to `mitigated`.

ThreatMitigationView.description:
One class of threat **this specific box** sees, the per-device
(positional) view, from the engine cascade. Distinct from the fleet-wide
`ThreatClassView`: `reaching` is what arrived at THIS box after upstream
defenders, not the fleet total, and `residual` is what this box passes on.

One row per class the box is IN THE PATH OF, defended or not. Rows are NOT
filtered on `capacity > 0`: a box that forwards a class it cannot (or
currently does not) defend still reports `reaching: N, mitigated: 0,
capacity: 0`. That is precisely the readout the player needs when they
switch a firewall off or run a class nothing on-prem defends, the old
filter blanked the console at the one moment exposure mattered. Use
`defense_capable` to tell the two zero-capacity cases apart.

Shared by `ApplianceView::threats` AND `GatewayView::threats`, both
security consoles render the SAME per-class mitigation row off this type,
so the gateway and appliance present threat detection/mitigation
identically.

capacity.description:
This box's own LIVE capacity for the class. `0` means nothing is being
stopped here right now, whatever the reason.

defense_capable.description:
Is this box BUILT to defend the class at all, a gateway's built-in
L3/L4 firewall for Protocol/Volumetric/Intrusion (plus any fitted
add-on's class), or an appliance SKU's base function / fittable
licenses. Independent of whether that defence is currently switched on.

The renderer needs it to word a `capacity == 0` row honestly:
- `true` → "defended, but switched off / unlicensed / this box is down"
  (actionable: turn it back on);
- `false` → "nothing here defends this class, it transits undefended"
  (actionable: buy the box that does, or nothing on-prem can help,
  the L7/Application case).

reaching.description: Threat (in the class unit) arriving at this box.

residual.description: Passed on (what this box couldn't catch).

active_ddos_mbps.description:
Live volumetric attack arriving on the wire, in **MEGABITS/s**.

Megabits rather than whole Gbps: a garage's entire threat surface is at
most its 1 Gbps circuit, so whole Gbps has no resolution at the tier
where most players meet the mechanic.

appliance_fabric_drop_p.description:
In-path appliance forwarding-drop probability from the LAST appliance
fabric pass: the worst (max) excess-over-effective-capacity fraction
across every saturated IN-PATH inspector that actually forwards,
clamped to `saturation_drop_cap`. 0 when none saturated. Mirrors
`Engine::traffic.appliance_fabric_drop_p`.

backbone_drop_p.description:
Inter-AZ backbone drop probability from the LAST backbone pass: the
fraction of cross-AZ traffic the regional fibre can't carry, clamped
to `saturation_drop_cap`. 0 when not saturated. Mirrors
`Engine::traffic.backbone_drop_p`: the MAX over every lane of every inter-zone
trunk (`az_trunks` carries the per-lane figures).

busiest_host_id.description:
The online host with the highest live CPU share
(`used_millivcpu / physical_vcpu`), 0 when there is none.

busiest_host_label.description:
That host's label, the same text as `HostView::label`, so a wall can
name it without holding the host rows.

busiest_host_load.description:
That host's live CPU share, 0..1 (may exceed 1.0 on an oversold box
that is being throttled; readers clamp for a bar).

cable_count.description:
Every cable in the world, and how many of them are failed right now
(`CableView::is_failed`): the fleet a cables meter shows.

contended_host_count.description:
Online hosts whose live demand exceeds their effective vCPU (the same
predicate as `HostView::contention_state == "contended"`).

current_progression_step.description:
0-indexed step rank of the current site in the scenario's
progression list. 0 if scenario has no progression. Drives UI
chrome (tutorial vs post-tutorial) and progression-step quest
gating on the renderer side.

current_site_id.description:
Stable id of the site the player is currently at (e.g. "garage",
"small_colo"). Display-name lookup goes via the catalog.

current_site_name.description: Display name for the current site (e.g. "Garage", "Datacenter").

east_west_gbps.description:
**Server-to-server traffic across the fleet, as a figure rather than a
remainder.**

Accumulated where east-west bytes are served (`ew_offer_and_deliver`)
as sender-egress plus receiver-ingress, so it is exactly what those
bytes contribute to `fabric_egress_gbps + fabric_ingress_gbps`, and
smoothed with the same half-life as its three neighbours.

Do not derive it as `fabric_egress + fabric_ingress - north_south`: that
holds only while the edge drops nothing, and a blocked flood drives the
subtraction negative.

fabric_egress_gbps.description:
Fleet aggregates folded ENGINE-SIDE in the same walk as
`online_host_count`. An off-console reader (the wall displays) reads a
global figure off the topbar or a `fleet:*` ring, never a client sweep
over the entity rows; the rows are the detail level. The console's own
fleet-level figures read these too, so a wall and the laptop can never
disagree.

Every host's NIC egress summed (the fabric traffic the Network page
heads with), world scope, every host whatever its state. The three
traffic readouts here sum per-device figures that the metrics sweep
already smooths, so they lag the instantaneous traffic by design and a
storage rebalance burst does not step the figure.

fabric_ingress_gbps.description:
Every host's NIC ingress summed, smoothed as above. `fabric_egress +
fabric_ingress` is the total the fabric carries; minus
`north_south_gbps` it is east-west.

fleet_disk_pct.description:
Disk used across online hosts, weighted by nameplate disk
(`HostView::ssd_used_pct` x the SKU's disk), 0..1.

fleet_mem_pct.description:
Live memory requested across online hosts, weighted by each host's
nameplate memory (`HostView::mem_requested_pct` x the SKU's memory,
over the nameplate sum), 0..1. The Capacity page's own rule.

inter_zone_gbps.description:
Traffic between the site's zones right now (Gbps): the sum of every
lane of every inter-zone trunk. Cross-zone
east-west, replication and egress failover all count; same-fabric
traffic never does. The wall's inter-building figure. Zero on a
single-zone site.

north_south_gbps.description:
What crosses the routers to and from the internet: every gateway's
`wan_egress_gbps + wan_ingress_gbps`, smoothed as above.

**Do not subtract this from the fabric pair to get east-west.** It
counts hostile inbound that ARRIVES at the edge, before mitigation
(`traffic/fabric.rs`, "a blocked flood reads ingress > egress"), while
the fabric pair are host-NIC sums that can only see what was actually
forwarded. Read `east_west_gbps` below instead.

online_host_count.description:
Hosts the engine calls serviceable right now: powered, up, AND
reachable through a live network chain to a carrier line
(`Engine::host_is_serviceable`, the same predicate `HostView::online`
mirrors per row). World scope, every session, every tick.

The HUD's "N hosts online" line reads this rather than folding over
every host row. The engine holds the reachable set memoised on
`topology_version`, so this is a lookup per host in Rust and nothing on
the client.

racked_host_count.description:
Hosts mounted in a rack (`HostView::inv_status == "Mounted"`), the
denominator under `online_host_count`; carried or boxed gear is not
a host that could be online.

staff_unlocked.description:
Whether staff hiring is available here (gated by site tier / scenario).
The client shows/hides the ops-console Staff tab off this: garage/
basement stay solo. See `Engine::staff_unlocked`.

total_cost_dollars.description:
`Engine::total_cost`: lifetime spend on what the business CONSUMED.

**This is OPERATING spend and EXCLUDES hardware purchases.** A purchase
converts cash into an asset rather than booking a cost, so buying $25k
of hosts moves this figure by nothing; it shows up in
`cost_breakdown.total_capex_dollars` and reaches the P&L gradually as
depreciation. A UI should label this operating cost, not "total cost",
and put capital beside it.

total_one_time_revenue_dollars.description:
Lifetime one-time (capex) revenue: signup bonuses + reservation
prepay credits. Excluded from the monthly-revenue projection.

total_recurring_revenue_dollars.description:
Lifetime recurring (opex) revenue: hourly customer billing
across all services. The dashboard surfaces this alongside
`total_one_time_revenue_dollars` so the player can see what
share of lifetime revenue was earned vs. paid up-front.

wan_binding.description:
WHICH term binds: `"Lines"` / `"GatewayFabric"` / `"InlineAppliance"`,
or `""` when nothing is deliverable at all. A bare ceiling explains
nothing: this is what turns "8 of 200 Gbps" into an actionable
sentence. Where zones disagree it names the term wasting the most line
capacity, which is the one worth acting on.

wan_drop_p_worst_az.description:
WAN egress drop probability from the LAST uplink pass, the WORST of
any AZ's own figure: the fraction of that AZ's offered egress that
can't get out its own lines, clamped to `saturation_drop_cap`. 0 when
no AZ is saturated. Mirrors the max of `Engine::traffic.wan_drop_p_by_az`.
There is no facility-level circuit (lines belong to an EDD, an EDD to
an AZ), so this is a worst-case SUMMARY figure, never a sum across AZs.

wan_effective_gbps.description:
THE facility WAN ceiling the sim actually enforces (Gbps), mirroring
`Engine::effective_wan_gbps`, the per-zone `min(lines, gateway fabric,
inline edge box)` summed over zones. Sustained egress above this is what
drives `wan_drop_p_worst_az` above.

`uplink_capacity_total_gbps` is the NAMEPLATE sum and is routinely far
larger: two 100 G circuits behind two non-BGP routers bill 200 and
deliver whatever the single largest router forwards. Show both so that
reads as a rule rather than a bug.

wan_gateway_fabric_gbps.description:
Σ router forwarding capacity after every fitted security add-on's
throttle, under the BGP law: advertising edges aggregate, and without
BGP a SINGLE router is the lone active edge (two non-BGP routers cannot
share a prefix). See `Engine::bgp_edge_fabric_gbps`: the rule is
deliberate, and naming it is this field's whole purpose.

wan_inline_appliance_gbps.description: Tightest racked in-path edge firewall, `min(ASIC, Σ bonded WAN ports)`.

wan_lines_gbps.description:
The three terms `wan_effective_gbps` is a min over, so the console can
show the comparison rather than an unexplained number.

`wan_lines_gbps` is Σ per-line effective circuit capacity (post
pairing-law, so a dark line reads 0). The other two are `0.0` when NOT
MODELLED and therefore not gating; `wan_binding` disambiguates, since it
never names a term that is absent rather than empty.

warm_host_count.description:
Online hosts past 80% of their effective vCPU but not contended
(`HostView::contention_state == "warm"`).

cable_count.description:
Number of cables currently routed through this tray segment.
Used by the renderer to compute bundle pitch (more cables → tighter
pitch up to the soft `bundle_capacity`, then a second row).

dark_reason.description:
Why the line is below nameplate: empty when fully live,
"not patched" (dark, zero capacity, `patched` is false), or
"patch slower than circuit" (throttled, `patched` stays true and
`effective_gbps` carries the throttled value).

effective_gbps.description:
Per-line effective throughput under the port-pairing law:
`min(circuit, patch deliverable, gateway side)`, see
`Engine::edd_line_effective_gbps`. 0.0 while the line is dark
(unpatched) or in carrier outage.

failed.description: `true` while the line is in transient carrier outage (no bandwidth).

patched.description:
`true` when the line's handoff port carries a live patch toward the
gateway (directly or via breakout legs).

priority.description: Sort key for fill order. Lower = filled first.

rx_saturated.description:
The ingress half. On an unbound line this also carries a volumetric
flood bigger than the wire, which the egress half never does.

saturated.description:
The line's live throughput (`egress_gbps` /
`ingress_gbps`, smoothed Gbps) is NOT on this view. It rides the
`edd:<id>:uplink:<n>:{egress_gbps, ingress_gbps}` metric subscription,
where `<n>` is this line's position in `EddView.uplinks`. A 4 Hz value
on a keyframe-only section would keep `edds` re-shipping on every
cadence keyframe for every session, console open or not.

Currently >= 100% of the line's group capacity in EITHER direction
(the engine's own edge, `metrics_uplink_pass`).

terminating_gateway_id.description:
`GatewayView::id` of the router this line's patch terminates on, or 0
when it resolves to none (dark, or a legacy unbound line).

The WAN policy is the ROUTER's decision and Active-Active shares a
plane only across the lines of ONE router, so two lines on the same
EDD can behave completely differently, and the EDD-level `wan_policy`
above cannot express that. Without this the Internet panel could not
tell the player why a live, patched, correctly-configured line carries
nothing: its router has no compute behind it. Same resolution the
distribution pass groups by (`Engine::edd_port_gateway_map_into`), so
the panel and the accounting can never disagree about which router owns
a line.

tx_saturated.description:
`saturated`, split by direction, set by the SAME `traffic/uplink.rs`
fold as `saturated` (the bound `SubscribedLine` fold's per-direction
threshold check, or the unbound facility waterfall's `full_e`/`full_i`).
`saturated == tx_saturated || rx_saturated`, always. Precedent shape
`AzTrunkView.ab_saturated`/`ba_saturated`.

wan_port_index.description:
Which EDD handoff port this line lands on. The Internet panel
targets Cancel / Upgrade by this index. `None` for legacy
facility-wide uplinks with no panel binding. (Field name kept for
wire compatibility.)

WorkloadRefView.description:
One placed workload that can be moved to another host: what
`MigrateWorkload` and `MigrateWorkloadToAz` name. Send `kind_tag`, `id`,
`host_id` (as `source_host_id`) and `unit_id` back exactly as they are here.

customer_id.description: The customer that owns the workload.

host_id.description: The host the workload is on now.

id.description:
The id the migrate commands check the workload against: the VM id for
"vm" and "db" (the same number as `unit_id`), the owning customer's id
for every other kind.

kind_tag.description:
The service it belongs to: "vm", "db", "obj", "cdn", "k8s" or "lb". A
managed database's backup storage is "obj".

unit_id.description:
The workload's own id. Unique across every service, and stable while the
workload exists.
